sentences.zh: 劉幽求劉幽求，冀州武強人也。

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu—Liu Youqiu was a native of Wuqiang in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu was a native of Wuqiang in Jizhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 聖歷年，應制舉，拜閬中尉，刺史不禮焉，乃棄官而歸。

translations.literal: In the Shengli era he entered an imperial special examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Langzhong, the prefect did not treat him with courtesy, and he abandoned his office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengli reign he entered an imperial special examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Langzhong. When the prefect failed to treat him with proper respect, he resigned his post and went home.

sentences.zh: 久之，授朝邑尉。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was appointed magistrate of Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed magistrate of Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 初，桓彥範、敬暉等雖誅張易之兄弟，竟不殺武三思。

translations.literal: At first, although Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, and others had executed the Zhang Yizhi brothers, in the end they did not kill Wu Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, though Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, and the others had put the Zhang Yizhi brothers to death, they ultimately failed to kill Wu Sansi.

sentences.zh: 幽求謂桓、敬曰：「三思尚存，公輩終無葬地。

translations.literal: Youqiu said to Huan and Jing, "With Sansi still alive, you gentlemen will in the end have no place for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu told Huan and Jing, "As long as Sansi remains alive, none of you will ever have a grave to rest in.

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，恐噬臍無及。

translations.literal: If you do not plan early, I fear it will be too late even to bite your navel in remorse.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not act soon, I fear you will regret it too late even to bite your own navel in anguish.

sentences.zh: 」桓、敬等不從其言，後果爲三思誣構，死於嶺外。

translations.literal: " Huan, Jing, and others did not follow his words; afterward they were indeed framed by Sansi and died beyond the Ling ranges.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan, Jing, and the others ignored his advice; in the end they were falsely accused by Sansi and perished in exile beyond the Ling mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 及韋庶人將行篡逆，幽求與玄宗潛謀誅之，乃與苑總監鍾紹京、長上果毅麻嗣宗及太平公主之子薛崇暕等夜從入禁中討平之。

translations.literal: When Consort Wei was about to carry out a usurpation, Youqiu secretly plotted with Emperor Xuanzong to execute her; together with Director of the Imperial Park Zhong Shaojing, changshang guoyi Ma Sizong, and Princess Taiping's son Xue Chongjian, among others, he entered the forbidden palace at night to suppress and pacify the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei was about to seize the throne, Youqiu secretly conspired with Prince Lin, the future Emperor Xuanzong, to overthrow her. That night he entered the inner palace with Zhong Shaojing, director of the imperial park, changshang guoyi Ma Sizong, Princess Taiping's son Xue Chongjian, and others, and together they put down the coup.

sentences.zh: 是夜所下制敕百餘道，皆出於幽求。

translations.literal: On that night, of the more than a hundred edicts and orders issued, all came from Youqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Of the more than a hundred edicts issued that night, every one was drafted by Youqiu.

sentences.zh: 以功擢拜中書舍人，令參知機務，賜爵中山縣男，食實封二百戸。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted and appointed as a drafter in the Secretariat, ordered to participate in confidential affairs, granted the title of Baron of Zhongshan county, with two hundred households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he was promoted to secretarial drafter and assigned to deliberations on state affairs. He was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhongshan, with an actual income fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又授其二子五品官，祖、父俱追贈刺史。

translations.literal: The next day, his two sons were also granted fifth-rank offices, and both his grandfather and father were posthumously enfeoffed as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: The next day his two sons were also given fifth-rank offices, and both his grandfather and father were posthumously honored as prefects.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，加銀青光祿大夫，行尚書右丞，仍舊知政事，進封徐國公，加實封通前五百戸，賜物千段、奴婢二十人、宅一區、地十頃、馬四匹，加以金銀雜器。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, Youqiu was given the additional title of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and continued to manage affairs of state; he was advanced to Duke of Xu state, with actual fief income brought to five hundred households in all, and was granted a thousand bolts of goods, twenty male and female servants, one residence, ten qing of land, four horses, and various gold, silver, and other vessels.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Youqiu was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while retaining his role in governance. He was advanced to Duke of Xu, with his actual fief income raised to five hundred households in all, and received a thousand bolts of silk and other goods, twenty servants, a residence, ten qing of land, four horses, and an assortment of gold and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: ，遷戸部尚書，罷知政事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue and removed from managing affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Minister of Revenue and removed from active participation in governance.

sentences.zh: 月餘，轉吏部尚書，擢拜侍中，降璽書曰：「頃者，王室不造，中宗厭代，外戚專政，奸臣擅國，將傾社稷，幾遷龜鼎，朕躬與王公，皆將及於禍難。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and promoted to Palace Attendant; an imperial letter was issued saying, "Recently the royal house suffered misfortune, Emperor Zhongzong passed from the throne, maternal relatives monopolized government, treacherous ministers seized the state, the altars of soil and grain were about to topple, and the imperial regalia nearly changed hands; I myself together with the princes and nobles were all about to meet with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and promoted to Palace Attendant. An imperial letter was issued that read, "Recently the royal house fell into misfortune. Emperor Zhongzong departed this life, maternal relatives monopolized power, treacherous ministers seized control of the state, the altars of soil and grain were nearly overturned, and the throne itself was almost lost. I, together with the princes and nobles, stood on the brink of disaster.

sentences.zh: 卿見危思奮，在變能通，翊贊儲君，協和義士，殄殲元惡，放殛兇徒。

translations.literal: You, seeing peril, thought to exert yourself; amid change you could adapt; you assisted and supported the heir apparent, harmonized with men of righteousness, exterminated the chief villain, and cast out and executed the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: You saw danger and resolved to act, adapted skillfully in the midst of upheaval, supported the heir apparent, rallied men of righteousness, destroyed the chief villain, and drove out the wicked.

sentences.zh: 我國家之復存，醫茲是賴，厥庸甚茂，朕用嘉焉。

translations.literal: That our state was restored to existence depends on healing such as this; your merit is very abundant, and I am pleased with it.
translations.idiomatic: Our state's restoration depended on service such as yours; your merit is great, and I am deeply gratified.

sentences.zh: 故委卿以衡軸，胙卿以茅土，然征賦未廣，寵錫猶輕。

translations.literal: Therefore I entrusted you with the pivot of government and enfeoffed you with feudal lands, yet the levies were not broad and the favors granted were still meager.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I entrusted you with the helm of state and enfeoffed you with feudal lands, yet the revenue attached to your fief was still limited and the honors bestowed upon you remained insufficient.

sentences.zh: 昔西漢行封，更擇多戸；

translations.literal: Formerly, when the Western Han carried out enfeoffments, it selected households in greater number;
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Han, when enfeoffments were granted, additional households were often chosen;

sentences.zh: 東京定賞，復增大邑。

translations.literal: when the Eastern Capital fixed rewards, it again enlarged the great fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: and when the Eastern Han fixed rewards, great fiefs were again enlarged.

sentences.zh: 故加賜卿實封二百戸，兼舊七百戸。

translations.literal: Therefore I additionally grant you two hundred households of actual fief income, together with the former seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly I am granting you an additional two hundred households of actual fief income, for seven hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 使夫高岸爲谷，長河如帶，子子孫孫，傳國無絕。

translations.literal: May high banks become valleys and long rivers become like ribbons; from sons to sons and grandsons to grandsons, may the transmission of the state never cease.
translations.idiomatic: May your line endure through the ages, from sons to grandsons without end, even as high banks become valleys and great rivers shrink to ribbons.

sentences.zh: 又以卿忘軀徇難，宜有恩榮，故特免卿十死罪，並書諸金鐵，俾傳於後。

translations.literal: Also, because you forgot your body and followed difficulty, you deserve grace and honor; therefore I specially exempt you from ten capital offenses, and record this on metal and iron so that it may be transmitted to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Because you risked your life in the crisis, you deserve special honor. I therefore grant you exemption from ten capital offenses, to be inscribed on metal and iron and passed down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 卿其保茲功業，永作國楨，可不美歟！

translations.literal: You should preserve this achievement and forever serve as a pillar of the state—is this not splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Preserve this achievement and remain forever a pillar of the state—could anything be finer!

sentences.zh: 先天元年，拜尚書右僕射、同中書門下三品，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the same rank as the Three Departments at the third grade, and overseer of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In 712 he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, given third-rank status equal to the chancellors, and charged with overseeing the national history.

sentences.zh: 幽求初自謂功在朝臣之右，而誌求左僕射，兼領中書令。

translations.literal: At first Youqiu considered his merit to rank above the other court ministers and sought the Left Vice Director post while also holding the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu initially believed his merit outranked that of the other court ministers and sought the post of Left Vice Director together with the directorship of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄而竇懷貞爲左僕射，崔湜爲中書令，幽求心甚不平，形於言色。

translations.literal: Before long Dou Huaizhen became Left Vice Director and Cui Shi became Director of the Secretariat; Youqiu's heart was very resentful, and this showed in his words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dou Huaizhen was made Left Vice Director and Cui Shi Director of the Secretariat. Youqiu was deeply resentful, and his displeasure showed plainly in his words and bearing.

sentences.zh: 湜又托附太平公主，將謀逆亂。

translations.literal: Shi moreover relied on and attached himself to Princess Taiping and was about to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi had also attached himself to Princess Taiping and was plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 幽求乃與右羽林將軍張暐請以羽林兵誅之，乃令暐密奏玄宗曰：「宰相中有崔湜、崔羲，俱是太平公主進用，見作方計，其事不輕。

translations.literal: Youqiu then joined with Right General of the Feathered Forest Zhang Wei in requesting that the Feathered Forest troops be used to execute them; he had Wei secretly report to Emperor Xuanzong, saying, "Among the chief ministers are Cui Shi and Cui Yi, both advanced by Princess Taiping; they are now making plans, and the matter is no light one.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu then joined Right General of the Feathered Forest Zhang Wei in proposing that the imperial guard be used to eliminate them. He had Wei secretly report to Emperor Xuanzong, "Among the chief ministers are Cui Shi and Cui Yi, both promoted by Princess Taiping. They are already plotting, and the matter is grave.

sentences.zh: 殿下若不早謀，必成大患。

translations.literal: If Your Highness does not plan early, it will surely become a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness does not act soon, this will surely become a grave disaster.

sentences.zh: 一朝事出意外，太上皇何以得安？

translations.literal: If in one morning affairs take an unexpected turn, how can the Retired Emperor be secure?
translations.idiomatic: If events take an unexpected turn, how will the Retired Emperor be kept safe?

sentences.zh: 古人云：『當斷不斷，反受其亂。

translations.literal: The ancients said, 'When one should decide but does not, one instead suffers disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said, 'He who ought to act decisively but fails to do so will suffer disorder in return.'

sentences.zh: 』唯請急殺此賊。

translations.literal: I beg only that these villains be urgently killed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that these traitors be put to death at once.

sentences.zh: 劉幽求已共臣作定謀計訖，願以身正此事，赴死如歸。

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu has already finished making plans with me; I wish to set this matter right with my own body and go to death as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu and I have already settled our plans. I am ready to see this through with my own life and go to my death as willingly as if I were going home.

sentences.zh: 臣既職典禁兵，若奉殿下命，當即除翦。

translations.literal: Since I am charged with command of the forbidden troops, if I receive Your Highness's order, I shall immediately eliminate and cut them down.
translations.idiomatic: As I command the palace guard, I shall cut them down at once upon receiving Your Highness's order.

sentences.zh: 」上深以爲然。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply convinced.

sentences.zh: 暐又泄其謀於侍御史鄧光賓，玄宗大懼，遽列上其狀，睿宗下幽求等詔獄，令法官推鞫之。

translations.literal: Wei also leaked the plot to Attending Censor Deng Guangbin; Emperor Xuanzong was greatly afraid and hurriedly submitted a full report of the matter; Emperor Ruizong sent Youqiu and the others to the imperial prison by edict and ordered the judges to investigate and interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also leaked the plot to Attending Censor Deng Guangbin. Emperor Xuanzong was greatly alarmed and immediately reported the whole affair. Emperor Ruizong sent Youqiu and the others to the imperial prison by edict and ordered the judges to investigate them.

sentences.zh: 法官奏幽求等以疏間親，罪當死。

translations.literal: The judges reported that Youqiu and the others, by estranging close kin, deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: The judges ruled that Youqiu and the others had driven a wedge between close kin and deserved death.

sentences.zh: 玄宗屢救獲免，乃流幽求於封州，暐於峰州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong repeatedly rescued them and they were spared; Youqiu was banished to Feng prefecture and Wei to Peak prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong repeatedly intervened on their behalf and saved them from execution. Youqiu was banished to Feng prefecture and Wei to Peak prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，太平公主等伏誅，其日下詔曰：「劉幽求風雲玄感，川嶽粹靈，學綜九流，文窮三變。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Princess Taiping and the others were executed; on that day an edict was issued saying, "Liu Youqiu was moved by wind and clouds and touched by dark mystery; rivers and mountains distilled his pure spirit; his learning embraced the nine schools, and his writing exhausted the three transformations.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Princess Taiping and her faction were executed. That same day an edict was issued: "Liu Youqiu was touched by heaven's signs and endowed with the pure spirit of mountains and rivers. His learning embraced all schools of thought, and his literary skill mastered every form of expression.

sentences.zh: 義以臨事，精能貫日；

translations.literal: In righteousness he faced affairs, and his keen ability pierced the sun;
translations.idiomatic: Righteous in action, his keen insight shone like the sun;

sentences.zh: 忠以成謀，用若投水。

translations.literal: in loyalty he completed plans, and in application he was like throwing into water.
translations.idiomatic: loyal in counsel, he acted with the swift certainty of a stone cast into water.

sentences.zh: 茂勛立艱難之際，嘉話盈啟沃之初，存讜直以不顧，爲奸邪之所忌。

translations.literal: Abundant merit was established in a time of hardship; fine words filled the beginning of counsel; he preserved direct remonstrance without regard for himself and was envied by treacherous villains.
translations.idiomatic: He won great merit in a time of peril and offered fine counsel at the founding of the new reign. He preserved honest remonstrance without regard for himself, and the wicked came to hate him for it.

sentences.zh: 釁萌頗露，譖端潛發，元宰見逐，讒人孔多。

translations.literal: The first signs of trouble were quite exposed, the beginnings of slander secretly arose, the chief minister was driven away, and slanderers were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The first signs of trouble appeared, slander began to spread in secret, the chief minister was driven out, and calumniators multiplied.

sentences.zh: 既殄群兇，方宣大化，期問政於經始，載登賢於蘿蔔。

translations.literal: Now that the wicked band has been exterminated, great transformation is about to be proclaimed; we expect to inquire about government at the beginning of the enterprise and to install the worthy as at the planting of radishes.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the villains have been destroyed and great reform is to be proclaimed, it is time to seek counsel at the founding of the new order and to restore the worthy to office.

sentences.zh: 可依舊金紫光祿大夫，守尚書左僕射，知軍國事，監修國史，上柱國、徐國公，仍依舊還封七百戸，並賜錦衣一襲。

translations.literal: He may according to precedent be restored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, managing military and state affairs, overseeing the compilation of the national history, Senior Pillar of the State and Duke of Xu, with his former fief of seven hundred households restored, and one suit of brocade robes granted as well.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be restored to his former rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with charge over military and state affairs and oversight of the national history, as Senior Pillar of the State and Duke of Xu. Let his former fief of seven hundred households be restored, and grant him one suit of brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 開元初，改尚書左右僕射爲左右丞相，乃授幽求尚書左丞相，兼黃門監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs were changed to Left and Right Chancellors; Youqiu was then appointed Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Director of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan reign the Left and Right Vice Directors were redesignated Left and Right Chancellors. Youqiu was appointed Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Director of the Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除太子少保，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and removed from managing affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and removed from active participation in governance.

sentences.zh: 姚崇素嫉忌之，乃奏言幽求郁怏於散職，兼有怨言，貶授睦州刺史，削其實封六百戸。

translations.literal: Yao Chong had long envied and resented him; he then memorialized that Youqiu was sullen in a vacant post and also had words of complaint, and Youqiu was demoted and appointed prefect of Mu, with six hundred households of his actual fief stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong had long envied him and memorialized that Youqiu was discontent in a powerless post and had voiced complaints. Youqiu was demoted to prefect of Mu, and six hundred households were stripped from his actual fief.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，稍遷杭州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was gradually transferred to prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉桂陽郡刺史，在道憤恚而卒，年六十一，贈禮部尚書，謚曰文獻，配享睿宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to prefect of Guiyang commandery; on the road he died in anger and resentment at age sixty-one; he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites, given the posthumous title Wenxian, and granted a place in the temple court of Emperor Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to prefect of Guiyang commandery but died on the road, embittered, at the age of sixty-one. He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites, given the posthumous title Wenxian, and granted a place in Emperor Ruizong's temple.

sentences.zh: ，重贈司徒。

translations.literal: He was again posthumously granted the title of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored again as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 鍾紹京鍾紹京，虔州贛人也。

translations.literal: Zhong Shaojing—Zhong Shaojing was a native of Gan in Qian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shaojing was a native of Gan in Qian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初爲司農録事，以工書直鳳閣，則天時明堂門額、九鼎之銘，及諸宮殿門榜，皆紹京所題。

translations.literal: At first he was a recorder in the Ministry of Agriculture; because of his skill in calligraphy he served directly in the Phoenix Pavilion; in Empress Wu's time the gate inscription of the Bright Hall, the inscriptions on the Nine Cauldrons, and the gate plaques of the various palaces were all written by Shaojing.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the Ministry of Agriculture. Because of his skill in calligraphy he served directly in the Phoenix Pavilion. During Empress Wu's reign the gate inscription of the Bright Hall, the inscriptions on the Nine Cauldrons, and the gate plaques of the various palaces were all written by Shaojing.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，爲苑總監。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he was Director of the Imperial Park.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong reign he served as director of the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 玄宗之誅韋氏，紹京夜中帥戸奴及丁夫以從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong executed the Wei clan, Shaojing at night led household slaves and corvée laborers to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong moved against the Wei clan, Shaojing led household slaves and corvée laborers to join him in the night.

sentences.zh: 及事成，其夜拜紹京銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎，參知機務。

translations.literal: When the affair was accomplished, that same night Shaojing was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Vice Director of the Secretariat, participating in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup succeeded, Shaojing was that same night appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Vice Director of the Secretariat, with a role in confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 翌日，進拜中書令，加光祿大夫，封越國公，賜實封五百戸，賜物二千段、馬十匹。

translations.literal: The next day he was advanced to Director of the Secretariat, given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Yue state, granted five hundred households of actual fief income, and given two thousand bolts of goods and ten horses.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, granted an actual income fief of five hundred households, and given two thousand bolts of silk and other goods and ten horses.

sentences.zh: 紹京既當朝用事，恣情賞罰，甚爲時人所惡。

translations.literal: Since Shaojing was now in power at court, he dispensed rewards and punishments according to his whim and was greatly hated by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shaojing held power at court, he dispensed rewards and punishments as he pleased and was widely despised.

sentences.zh: 俄又抗疏讓官，睿宗納薛稷之言，乃轉爲戸部尚書，出爲蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he also submitted a memorial refusing office; Emperor Ruizong accepted Xue Ji's advice and transferred him to Minister of Revenue, then sent him out as prefect of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he submitted a memorial declining his office. Emperor Ruizong heeded Xue Ji's advice and transferred him to Minister of Revenue, then sent him out as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，復召拜戸部尚書，遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Shaojing was again summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue, then transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Shaojing was again summoned as Minister of Revenue and then transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時姚崇素惡紹京之爲人，因奏紹京發言怨望，左遷綿州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Chong had long disliked Shaojing's character; he therefore memorialized that Shaojing spoke words of resentment and complaint, and Shaojing was demoted to prefect of Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong had long disliked Shaojing's character and memorialized that he had spoken resentfully. Shaojing was demoted to prefect of Mian.

sentences.zh: 及坐事，累貶琰川尉，盡削其階爵及實封。

translations.literal: When he was implicated in an offense, he was repeatedly demoted to assistant magistrate of Yanchuan, and all his ranks, titles, and actual fief income were stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: After he became implicated in an offense, he was repeatedly demoted until he reached the post of assistant magistrate of Yanchuan, and all his ranks, titles, and actual fief income were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 俄又歷遷溫州別駕。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred in turn to vice prefect of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to vice prefect of Wen.

sentences.zh: ，入朝，因垂泣奏曰：「陛下豈不記疇昔之事耶？

translations.literal: He entered court and, weeping, memorialized, saying, "Does Your Majesty not remember affairs of days past?
translations.idiomatic: He came to court and, weeping, memorialized, "Does Your Majesty not remember what happened in those days?

sentences.zh: 何忍棄臣荒外，永不見闕庭。

translations.literal: How can you bear to abandon me in the wilds beyond the frontier, never again to see the court of the palace gate?
translations.idiomatic: How can you bear to cast me off in the wilderness beyond the frontier, never again to see the imperial court?

sentences.zh: 且當時立功之人，今並亡歿，唯臣衰老獨在，陛下豈不垂湣耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, of those who achieved merit at that time, all have now died; only I, old and aged, remain alone—does Your Majesty not show pity?
translations.idiomatic: Of those who won merit in those days, all have now died. I alone remain, old and frail. Will Your Majesty not show me compassion?

sentences.zh: 」玄宗爲之惘然，即日拜銀青光祿大夫、右諭德。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanzong was moved with sorrow for him and that same day appointed him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanzong was deeply moved and that same day appointed him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉少詹事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘卒。

translations.literal: At over eighty years of age he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at over eighty years of age.

sentences.zh: 紹京雅好書畫古跡，聚二王及褚遂良書至數十百卷。

translations.literal: Shaojing elegantly loved books, paintings, and ancient traces; he collected writings by the Two Wangs and Chu Suiliang to the number of several tens or hundreds of scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing was a devoted collector of calligraphy, painting, and antiquities, amassing several dozen or even several hundred scrolls by the Two Wangs and Chu Suiliang.

sentences.zh: ，重贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: He was again posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored again as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 郭元振郭元振，魏州貴鄉人。

translations.literal: Guo Yuanzhen—Guo Yuanzhen was a native of Guixiang in Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuanzhen was a native of Guixiang in Wei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，授通泉尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Tongquan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Tongquan.

sentences.zh: 任俠使氣，不以細務介意，前後掠賣所部千餘人，以遺賓客，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: He was chivalrous and bold in spirit, did not concern himself with minor affairs, and before and after seized and sold more than a thousand people under his jurisdiction to give to guests; the common people suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and chivalrous by nature, he paid little heed to minor duties. He seized and sold more than a thousand people under his jurisdiction to entertain guests, to the great suffering of the common people.

sentences.zh: 則天聞其名，召見與語，甚奇之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu heard his name, summoned him for an audience and conversation, and considered him very remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu heard of him, summoned him for an audience, and was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃請和，乃授元振右武衞鎧曹，充使聘於吐蕃。

translations.literal: At that time the Tibetans requested peace, and Yuanzhen was appointed Armor Bureau officer of the Right Martial Guard and sent as envoy on a mission to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans requested peace, Yuanzhen was appointed an officer of the Right Martial Guard's Armor Bureau and sent as envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大將論欽陵請去四鎮兵，分十姓之地，朝廷使元振因察其事宜。

translations.literal: The Tibetan general Lun Qinling requested the removal of troops from the Four Garrisons and the division of the lands of the Ten Surnames; the court sent Yuanzhen to investigate the circumstances of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan general Lun Qinling requested the withdrawal of troops from the Four Garrisons and a division of the lands of the Ten Surnames. The court sent Yuanzhen to investigate the matter on the spot.

sentences.zh: 元振還，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yuanzhen returned and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen returned and submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 則天從之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 又上言曰：「臣揣吐蕃百姓倦徭戍久矣，咸願早和。

translations.literal: He also submitted a statement saying, "Your subject surmises that the Tibetan common people have long been weary of corvée and frontier service and all wish for early peace.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial saying, "I believe the Tibetan people have long grown weary of corvée labor and frontier service, and all wish for peace as soon as possible.

sentences.zh: 其大將論欽陵欲分四鎮境，統兵專制，故不欲歸款。

translations.literal: Their general Lun Qinling wishes to divide the territory of the Four Garrisons and monopolize command of the troops, and therefore does not wish to submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Their general Lun Qinling wishes to carve up the territory of the Four Garrisons and monopolize military command, and therefore does not wish to submit.

sentences.zh: 若國家每歳發和親使，而欽陵常不從命，則彼蕃之人怨欽陵日深，望國恩日甚，設欲廣舉醜徒，固亦難矣。

translations.literal: If the state each year sends marriage-alliance envoys and Qinling constantly does not follow orders, then the people of that foreign land will resent Qinling daily more deeply and look to the state's grace daily more intensely; even if he wished to raise a broad host of wicked followers, it would indeed be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: If the court sends marriage-alliance envoys every year and Qinling repeatedly refuses to comply, the Tibetan people will resent him more deeply by the day and look to the court's favor more eagerly. Even if he wished to raise a large army, it would be difficult.

sentences.zh: 斯亦離間之漸，必可使其上下俱懷情阻。

translations.literal: This is also a gradual method of sowing discord; it will surely be able to make both superiors and subordinates harbor obstructive feelings.
translations.idiomatic: This would also be a gradual means of sowing discord and would surely make both rulers and subjects estranged from one another.

sentences.zh: 」則天甚然之。

translations.literal: " Empress Wu considered this very correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是數年間，吐蕃君臣果相猜貳，因誅大將論欽陵。

translations.literal: From this, within several years, the Tibetan ruler and ministers indeed became mutually suspicious and divided, and the great general Lun Qinling was executed as a result.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the Tibetan ruler and his ministers did indeed become mutually suspicious, and the great general Lun Qinling was executed.

sentences.zh: 其弟贊婆及兄子莽布支並來降，則天仍令元振與河源軍大使夫蒙令卿率騎以接之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zanpo and his elder brother's son Mangbuzhi both came to surrender; Empress Wu still ordered Yuanzhen and the envoy of the Heyuan Army, Fumeng Lingqing, to lead cavalry to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zanpo and his elder brother's son Mangbuzhi both came to surrender. Empress Wu ordered Yuanzhen and Fumeng Lingqing, commander of the Heyuan Army, to lead cavalry to receive them.

sentences.zh: 後吐蕃將麹莽布支率兵入寇，涼州都督唐休璟勒兵破之。

translations.literal: Later the Tibetan general Qu Mangbuzhi led troops in an incursion; Tang Xiujing, military governor of Liang, mustered troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Tibetan general Qu Mangbuzhi led troops in a raid. Tang Xiujing, military governor of Liang, mustered troops and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 元振參預其謀，以功拜主客郎中。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen participated in planning the campaign; for his merit he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen took part in planning the campaign and, for his services, was appointed Director in the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 大足元年，遷涼州都督、隴右諸軍州大使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazu he was transferred to military governor of Liang and grand envoy of the army prefectures of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In 701 he was transferred to military governor of Liang and grand envoy over the army prefectures of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 先是，涼州封界南北不過四百餘里，既逼突厥、吐蕃，二寇頻歳奄至城下，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Before this, the boundaries of Liang from north to south extended no more than four hundred-odd li; since it pressed against the Turks and Tibetans, the two enemies frequently each year suddenly arrived beneath the city walls, and the common people suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Liang's territory extended no more than four hundred-odd li from north to south. Pressed by the Turks and Tibetans, the two foes frequently appeared each year beneath the city walls, and the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 元振始於南境破口置和戎城，北界磧中置白亭軍，控其要路，乃拓州境一千五百里，自是寇虜不復更至城下。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen first established Hecheng City at Pokou on the southern border and Baiting Army in the desert on the northern frontier, controlling the critical routes; he then expanded the prefecture's territory by one thousand five hundred li, and from this the raiding barbarians no longer again reached beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen first built Hecheng City at Pokou on the southern border and established Baiting Army in the northern desert to control the key routes. He expanded the prefecture's territory by fifteen hundred li, and from then on the raiders no longer reached the city walls.

sentences.zh: 元振又令甘州刺史李漢通開置屯田，盡其水陸之利。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen also ordered Li Hantong, prefect of Gan, to open and establish garrison farms and exhaust the advantages of water and land.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen also ordered Li Hantong, prefect of Gan, to establish garrison farms and make full use of the region's water and land.

sentences.zh: 舊涼州粟斛售至數千，及漢通收率之後，數年豐稔，乃至一匹絹粟數十斛，積軍糧支數十年。

translations.literal: Formerly in Liang a hu of grain sold for as much as several thousand; after Hantong collected and gathered harvests, within several years there was abundant yield, until one bolt of silk could buy several tens of hu of grain, and military grain was accumulated sufficient for several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a hu of grain in Liang sold for thousands of cash. After Hantong organized the harvests, within a few years the land grew abundant, until a bolt of silk could buy dozens of hu of grain and enough military grain was stored to supply the army for decades.

sentences.zh: 元振風神偉壯，而善於撫御，在涼州五年，夷夏畏慕，令行禁止，牛羊被野，路不拾遺。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen's bearing and spirit were grand and strong, and he was good at comforting and controlling; during five years in Liang, both barbarians and Chinese feared and admired him, orders were carried out and prohibitions enforced, cattle and sheep covered the wilds, and no one picked up lost objects on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was imposing in bearing and skilled at winning loyalty. During his five years in Liang, both barbarians and Chinese feared and admired him. His orders were obeyed, cattle and sheep covered the fields, and no one picked up lost objects on the roads.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，遷左驍衞將軍，兼檢校安西大都護。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era he was transferred to General of the Left Valiant Guard and concurrently acting Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong reign he was transferred to General of the Left Valiant Guard and concurrently acting Protector-General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 時西突厥首領烏質勒部落強盛，款塞通和，元振就其牙帳計會軍事。

translations.literal: At that time the chieftain of the Western Turks, Wuzhile, had a powerful tribe; he came to the frontier in good faith seeking peace, and Yuanzhen went to his royal tent to plan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Western Turk chieftain Wuzhile commanded a powerful tribe and came to the frontier seeking peace. Yuanzhen went to his royal tent to discuss military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時天大雪，元振立於帳前，與烏質勒言議。

translations.literal: At that time heaven snowed heavily; Yuanzhen stood before the tent and discussed matters with Wuzhile.
translations.idiomatic: It was snowing heavily. Yuanzhen stood before the tent and spoke with Wuzhile.

sentences.zh: 須臾，雪深風凍，元振未嘗移足，烏質勒年老，不勝寒苦，會罷而死。

translations.literal: Before long the snow was deep and the wind freezing; Yuanzhen never moved his feet, but Wuzhile was old and could not bear the cold hardship; when the meeting ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the snow had deepened and the wind turned bitterly cold. Yuanzhen never shifted his feet, but Wuzhile was old and could not endure the cold. When the meeting ended, he died.

sentences.zh: 其子娑葛以元振故殺其父，謀勒兵攻之。

translations.literal: His son Suoge, because Yuanzhen had caused his father's death, plotted to muster troops and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge, Wuzhile's son, believed Yuanzhen had caused his father's death and plotted to raise troops and attack him.

sentences.zh: 副使御史中丞解琬知其謀，勸元振夜遁，元振曰：「吾以誠信待人，何所疑懼，且深在寇庭，遁將安適？

translations.literal: The deputy envoy, Censor-in-Chief Jie Wan, learned of the plot and urged Yuanzhen to flee by night. Yuanzhen said, "I treat others with sincerity and trust—what is there to doubt or fear? Moreover, I am deep in the enemy camp; if I flee, where would I go?
translations.idiomatic: The deputy envoy, Censor-in-Chief Jie Wan, learned of the plot and urged Yuanzhen to flee by night. Yuanzhen replied, "I deal with others in good faith—what have I to fear? Besides, I am deep in the enemy's territory; where could I flee?

sentences.zh: 」乃安臥帳中。

translations.literal: " He then lay down peacefully in the tent.
translations.idiomatic: " He then lay down calmly in his tent.

sentences.zh: 明日，親入虜帳，哭之甚哀，行吊贈之禮。

translations.literal: The next day he personally entered the barbarian tent, wept with great grief, and performed the rites of mourning and condolence gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he entered the tent in person, wept bitterly, and performed the rites of mourning and condolence.

sentences.zh: 娑葛乃感其義，復與元振通好，因遣使進馬五千匹及方物。

translations.literal: Suoge was moved by his righteousness and restored friendly relations with Yuanzhen; he then sent envoys presenting five thousand horses and local products.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge was moved by his conduct and restored friendly relations with Yuanzhen, sending envoys with five thousand horses and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 制以元振爲金山道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: By imperial order Yuanzhen was made Grand Commander on Campaign of the Jinshan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order appointed Yuanzhen Grand Commander on Campaign of the Jinshan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 先是，娑葛與阿史那闕啜忠節不和，屢相侵掠。

translations.literal: Before this, Suoge and Ashina Quechuo Zhongjie were not on good terms and repeatedly raided one another.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Suoge and Ashina Quechuo Zhongjie had been at odds and repeatedly raided each other's territory.

sentences.zh: 闕啜兵眾寡弱，漸不能支。

translations.literal: Quechuo's troops were few and weak, and he gradually could not hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Quechuo's forces were few and weak, and he gradually found himself unable to hold out.

sentences.zh: 元振奏請追闕啜入朝宿衞，移其部落入於瓜、沙等州安置，制從之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen memorialized requesting that Quechuo be summoned to court to serve in the palace guard and that his tribe be moved and settled in Guazhou, Shazhou, and other prefectures; the order followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen memorialized asking that Quechuo be summoned to court for palace guard duty and that his tribe be resettled in Guazhou, Shazhou, and other prefectures. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 闕啜行至播仙城，與經略使、右威衞將軍周以悌相遇，以悌謂之曰：「國家有以高班厚秩待君者，以君統攝部落，下有兵眾故也。

translations.literal: When Quechuo reached Boxian City he met the frontier commissioner and General of the Right Martial Guard Zhou Yiti, who said to him, "The state treats you with high rank and generous stipends because you command a tribe and have troops under you.
translations.idiomatic: When Quechuo reached Boxian City he met the frontier commissioner and General of the Right Martial Guard Zhou Yiti, who told him, "The court honors you with high rank and generous stipends because you command a tribe with soldiers under you.

sentences.zh: 今輕身入朝，是一老胡耳，在朝之人，誰復喜見？

translations.literal: If you now go to court alone, you are merely an old barbarian—who at court would be glad to see you?
translations.idiomatic: If you go to court alone now, you will be nothing but an old barbarian—who at court will be glad to see you?

sentences.zh: 非唯官資難得，亦恐性命在人。

translations.literal: Not only will rank and salary be hard to obtain, but I fear your life will be in others' hands.
translations.idiomatic: Not only will you find rank and salary hard to obtain, but your very life may be in others' hands.

sentences.zh: 今宰相有宗楚客、紀處訥，並專權用事，何不厚貺二公，請留不行。

translations.literal: Now the chief ministers Zong Chuke and Ji Chune both monopolize power; why not give them rich gifts and ask to stay and not go?
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers Zong Chuke and Ji Chune now monopolize power. Why not give them rich gifts and ask to remain instead of going?

sentences.zh: 仍發安西兵並引吐蕃以擊娑葛，求阿史那獻爲可汗以招十姓，使郭虔瓘往拔汗那征甲馬以助軍用。

translations.literal: Then dispatch Anxi troops and bring in the Tibetans to attack Suoge, seek Ashina Xian as khan to win over the Ten Surnames, and send Guo Qian'gu to Ferghana to levy armor and horses to aid military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Then raise the Anxi troops and bring in the Tibetans to attack Suoge, install Ashina Xian as khan to win over the Ten Surnames, and send Guo Qian'gu to Ferghana to levy armor and horses for the army.

sentences.zh: 既得報讎，又得存其部落。

translations.literal: You will both obtain revenge and preserve your tribe.
translations.idiomatic: You will both have your revenge and keep your tribe intact.

sentences.zh: 如此，與入朝受制於人，豈復同也！

translations.literal: In this way, compared with entering court and being controlled by others, how could it be the same!
translations.idiomatic: That would be nothing like entering court and placing yourself at others' mercy!

sentences.zh: 」闕啜然其言，便勒兵攻陷於闐坎城，獲金寶及生口，遣人間道納賂於宗、紀。

translations.literal: " Quechuo considered his words correct, then mustered troops and captured Khotan Kan City, obtaining gold, jewels, and captives, and sent men by secret routes to offer bribes to Zong and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " Quechuo agreed, mustered troops, and captured Khotan Kan City, seizing gold, jewels, and captives. He then sent men by secret routes to bribe Zong and Ji.

sentences.zh: 元振聞其謀，遽上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yuanzhen heard of the plot and hurriedly submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhen learned of the plot, he immediately submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but ignored.

sentences.zh: 楚客等既受闕啜之賂，乃建議遣攝御史中丞馮嘉賓持節安撫闕啜，御史呂守素處置四鎮，持璽書便報元振。

translations.literal: Since Chuke and the others had received Quechuo's bribes, they proposed sending Acting Censor-in-Chief Feng Jiabin with credentials to pacify Quechuo, Censor Lu Shousu to manage the Four Garrisons, and an envoy bearing the imperial seal to report at once to Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: After Chuke and his faction accepted Quechuo's bribes, they proposed sending Acting Censor-in-Chief Feng Jiabin with credentials to pacify Quechuo, Censor Lu Shousu to manage the Four Garrisons, and an envoy bearing the imperial seal to notify Yuanzhen at once.

sentences.zh: 除牛師獎爲安西副都護，便領甘、涼已西兵募，兼征吐蕃，以討娑葛。

translations.literal: Niu Shijiang was appointed Vice Protector of Anxi and immediately led recruitment of troops west of Gan and Liang, also summoning the Tibetans, to attack Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Shijiang was appointed Vice Protector of Anxi and immediately took command of recruitment west of Gan and Liang, also calling in the Tibetans, to attack Suoge.

sentences.zh: 娑葛進馬使娑臘知楚客計，馳還報娑葛。

translations.literal: Suoge's horse-presenting envoy Sula learned of Chuke's plan and galloped back to report to Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge's envoy Sula, who had come to present horses, learned of Chuke's plan and galloped back to warn Suoge.

sentences.zh: 娑葛是日發兵五千騎出安西，五千騎出撥換，五千騎出焉耆，五千騎出疏勒。

translations.literal: That same day Suoge dispatched five thousand cavalry from Anxi, five thousand from Bochuan, five thousand from Yanqi, and five thousand from Shule.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Suoge dispatched five thousand cavalry from Anxi, five thousand from Bochuan, five thousand from Yanqi, and five thousand from Shule.

sentences.zh: 時元振在疏勒，於河口柵不敢動。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanzhen was at Shule and did not dare move from the stockade at the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was then at Shule and did not dare move from the stockade at the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 闕啜在計舒河口候見嘉賓，娑葛兵掩至，生擒闕啜，殺嘉賓等。

translations.literal: Quechuo waited at the mouth of the Jishu River to meet Jiabin; Suoge's troops suddenly arrived, captured Quechuo alive, and killed Jiabin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Quechuo waited at the mouth of the Jishu River to meet Jiabin, but Suoge's troops fell upon him, captured Quechuo alive, and killed Jiabin and his party.

sentences.zh: 呂守素至僻城，亦見害。

translations.literal: When Lu Shousu reached Picheng he was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shousu was also killed when he reached Picheng.

sentences.zh: 又殺牛師獎於火燒城，乃陷安西，四鎮路絕。

translations.literal: Niu Shijiang was also killed at Huoshao City; Anxi then fell and the routes to the Four Garrisons were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Shijiang was killed at Huoshao City as well. Anxi fell, and the routes to the Four Garrisons were severed.

sentences.zh: 楚客又奏請周以悌代元振統眾，征元振，將陷之。

translations.literal: Chuke again memorialized requesting that Zhou Yiti replace Yuanzhen in commanding the troops, summoning Yuanzhen back with the intent to entrap him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke again memorialized asking that Zhou Yiti replace Yuanzhen in command, summoning Yuanzhen back with the intent to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 使阿史那獻爲十姓可汗，置軍焉耆以取娑葛。

translations.literal: Ashina Xian was made khan of the Ten Surnames, and troops were stationed at Yanqi to capture Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Xian was installed as khan of the Ten Surnames, and troops were stationed at Yanqi to capture Suoge.

sentences.zh: 娑葛遺元振書曰：「與漢本來無惡，只讎於闕啜。

translations.literal: Suoge sent a letter to Yuanzhen saying, "With the Han we originally had no enmity; our grievance is only against Quechuo.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge wrote to Yuanzhen, "We bear the Han no ill will; our quarrel is only with Quechuo.

sentences.zh: 而宗尚書取闕啜金，枉擬破奴部落，馮中丞、牛都護相次而來，奴等豈坐受死！

translations.literal: Yet Minister Zong took Quechuo's gold and falsely plotted to destroy my tribe; Vice Censor Feng and Commander Niu came one after another—are we to sit and accept death!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Minister Zong took Quechuo's gold and plotted falsely to destroy my tribe. Vice Censor Feng and Commander Niu came one after another—are we to sit and await death?

sentences.zh: 又聞史獻欲來，徒擾亂軍州，恐未有寧日，乞大使商量處置。

translations.literal: I also hear that Shi Xian wishes to come, which would only disturb the army prefectures; I fear there will be no day of peace— I beg the envoy to discuss and settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that Ashina Xian is coming, which will only disturb the frontier prefectures. I fear there will never be peace. I beg the envoy to discuss a settlement.

sentences.zh: 」元振奏娑葛狀。

translations.literal: " Yuanzhen memorialized Suoge's account.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanzhen reported Suoge's letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 楚客怒，奏言元振有異圖。

translations.literal: Chuke was angry and memorialized that Yuanzhen had ulterior designs.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke was enraged and memorialized that Yuanzhen harbored treacherous intent.

sentences.zh: 元振使其子鴻間道奏其狀，以悌竟得罪，流於白州。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen had his son Hong report the situation by a secret route; Zhou Yiti ultimately was found guilty and banished to Baizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen sent his son Hong by a secret route to report the full situation. Zhou Yiti was ultimately found guilty and banished to Baizhou.

sentences.zh: 復以元振代以悌，赦娑葛罪，冊爲十四姓可汗。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen was again put in Zhou Yiti's place; Suoge's crimes were pardoned and he was enfeoffed as khan of the Fourteen Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was restored in Zhou Yiti's place. Suoge was pardoned and enfeoffed as khan of the Fourteen Surnames.

sentences.zh: 元振奏稱西土未寧，事資安撫，逗遛不敢歸京師。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen memorialized that the western lands were not yet settled and required pacification; he lingered and did not dare return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen reported that the western frontier was still unsettled and required pacification. He lingered on duty and did not dare return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會楚客等被誅，睿宗即位，征拜太仆卿，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Chuke and the others were executed and Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, Yuanzhen was summoned and appointed Minister of the Stud, with the additional title of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuke and his faction were executed and Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Yuanzhen was summoned as Minister of the Stud and given the additional title of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: ，同中書門下三品，代宋璟爲吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was given third-rank status equal to the chancellors and replaced Song Jing as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was given third-rank status equal to the chancellors and replaced Song Jing as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉兵部尚書，封館陶縣男。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Minister of War and enfeoffed as Baron of Guantao county.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Minister of War and enfeoffed as Baron of Guantao.

sentences.zh: 時元振父愛年老在鄉，就拜濟州刺史，仍聽致仕。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanzhen's father Ai was old and living in the countryside; he was appointed on the spot as prefect of Ji and permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuanzhen's father Ai was elderly and living at home. He was appointed prefect of Ji on the spot and permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 其冬，與韋安石、張説等俱罷知政事。

translations.literal: That winter he, together with Wei Anshi, Zhang Yue, and others, was all removed from managing affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was removed from governance together with Wei Anshi, Zhang Yue, and others.

sentences.zh: ，爲朔方軍大總管，始築定遠城，以爲行軍計集之所，至今賴之。

translations.literal: He became Grand Commander of the Shuofang Army and first built Dingyuan City as a place for assembling campaign plans; to this day it is relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Commander of the Shuofang Army and first built Dingyuan City as a base for campaign planning, a fortification still relied upon today.

sentences.zh: 明年，復同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: The next year he again received third-rank status equal to the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again received third-rank status equal to the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 及蕭至忠、竇懷貞等附太平公主潛謀不順，玄宗發羽林兵誅之，睿宗登承天門，元振躬率兵侍衞之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Zhizhong, Dou Huaizhen, and others attached themselves to Princess Taiping and secretly plotted rebellion, Emperor Xuanzong dispatched the Feathered Forest troops to execute them; Emperor Ruizong ascended Chengtian Gate, and Yuanzhen personally led troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Zhizhong, Dou Huaizhen, and others attached themselves to Princess Taiping and secretly plotted rebellion, Emperor Xuanzong dispatched the imperial guard to execute them. Emperor Ruizong ascended Chengtian Gate, and Yuanzhen personally led troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 事定論功，進封代國公，食實封四百戸，賜物一千段。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled and merit was assessed, he was advanced to Duke of Dai state, granted four hundred households of actual fief income, and given a thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled and merits were assessed, he was advanced to Duke of Dai, granted an actual income fief of four hundred households, and given a thousand bolts of silk and other goods.

sentences.zh: 又令兼御史大夫，持節爲朔方道大總管，以備突厥，未行。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to serve concurrently as Censor-in-Chief and, bearing credentials, to become Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit to guard against the Turks, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to serve concurrently as Censor-in-Chief and, bearing credentials, to become Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit to guard against the Turks, but he never departed.

sentences.zh: 玄宗於驪山講武，坐軍容不整，坐於纛下，將斬以徇，劉幽求、張説於馬前諫曰：「元振有翊贊大功，雖有罪，當從原宥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong held military exercises at Mount Li, Yuanzhen sat beneath the banner for disorderly military appearance and was about to be beheaded as an example; Liu Youqiu and Zhang Yue remonstrated before his horse, saying, "Yuanzhen has great merit in assisting and supporting the throne; though guilty, he should be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong held military exercises at Mount Li, Yuanzhen was seated beneath the command banner for disorderly troops and was about to be beheaded as an example. Liu Youqiu and Zhang Yue remonstrated before the emperor's horse, saying, "Yuanzhen rendered great service in supporting the throne. Though guilty, he should be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」乃赦之，流於新州。

translations.literal: " He was then pardoned and banished to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was pardoned but banished to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋又思其舊功，起爲饒州司馬。

translations.literal: Before long, remembering his former merit, the emperor recalled him and appointed him military aide of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, remembering his former services, the emperor recalled him and appointed him military aide of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 元振自恃功勛，怏怏不得誌，道病卒。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen, relying on his achievements, was resentful and unable to fulfill his ambitions; he died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen, confident in his achievements, was resentful and unable to achieve his ambitions. He died of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: ，追贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected writings in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 張説張説，字道濟，其先范陽人，代居河東，近又徙家河南之洛陽。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue—Zhang Yue, style name Daoji, his ancestors were men of Fanyang; for generations they lived in Hedong, and recently the family moved again to Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, whose courtesy name was Daoji, came from a Fanyang family that had lived for generations in Hedong and had recently moved to Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 弱冠應詔舉，對策乙第，授太子校書，累轉右補闕，預修《三教珠英》。

translations.literal: At age twenty he entered an imperial examination by edict, placed second in the policy response, was appointed collator to the Heir Apparent, was promoted in turn to Remonstrance on the Right, and participated in compiling the Three Teachings Pearl of Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered an imperial examination by edict, placed second in the policy response, and was appointed collator to the Heir Apparent. He rose in turn to Remonstrance on the Right and took part in compiling the Three Teachings Pearl of Excellence.

sentences.zh: 久視年，則天幸三陽宮，自夏涉秋，不時還都，説上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: In the Jiushi year Empress Wu visited the Sanyang Palace; from summer through autumn she did not return to the capital in timely fashion, and Yue submitted a remonstrance memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In 700 Empress Wu visited the Sanyang Palace. From summer through autumn she did not return to the capital on time, and Yue submitted a remonstrance memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but ignored.

sentences.zh: 長安初，修《三教珠英》畢，遷右史、內供奉，兼知考功貢舉事，擢拜鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chang'an era, when compilation of the Three Teachings Pearl of Excellence was completed, he was transferred to Right Historiographer and inner attendant, concurrently managing examination and tribute selection affairs, and was promoted to Phoenix Pavilion Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chang'an reign, when compilation of the Three Teachings Pearl of Excellence was completed, he was transferred to Right Historiographer and inner attendant, placed in charge of examination and tribute selection, and promoted to Phoenix Pavilion Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時臨臺監張易之與其弟昌宗構陷御史大夫魏元忠，稱其謀反，引説令證其事。

translations.literal: At that time Director of the Lin Platform Zhang Yizhi and his brother Changzong framed Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong, claiming he plotted rebellion, and summoned Yue to testify to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yizhi, Director of the Lin Platform, and his brother Changzong framed Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong on charges of rebellion and summoned Yue to testify.

sentences.zh: 説至御前，揚言元忠實不反，此是易之誣構耳。

translations.literal: When Yue came before the emperor, he declared openly that Yuanzhong in fact did not rebel and that this was Yizhi's false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue came before the throne, he declared openly that Yuanzhong had not rebelled and that this was Yizhi's false accusation.

sentences.zh: 元忠由是免誅，説坐忤旨配流欽州。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong thereby escaped execution; Yue, for opposing the imperial will, was sentenced to exile in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong thereby escaped execution. Yue, for opposing the imperial will, was exiled to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 在嶺外歳餘。

translations.literal: He remained beyond the Ling ranges for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in exile beyond the Ling ranges for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，召拜兵部員外郎，累轉工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, Yue was summoned and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of War, then promoted in turn to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Yue was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of War and later promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，丁母憂去職，起復授黃門侍郎，累表固辭，言甚切至，優詔方許之。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he left office upon his mother's death, was recalled from mourning and appointed Vice Director of the Palace Gate, repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining, spoke with great earnestness, and only after an gracious edict was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong reign he left office to mourn his mother. When recalled and appointed Vice Director of the Palace Gate, he repeatedly memorialized to decline, speaking with great earnestness, until an gracious edict finally allowed him to refuse.

sentences.zh: 是時風教紊類，多以起復爲榮，而説固節懇辭，竟終其喪制，大爲識者所稱。

translations.literal: At that time customs were disordered and many regarded recall from mourning as an honor, but Yue steadfastly declined and ultimately completed the full mourning period, greatly praised by discerning men.
translations.idiomatic: At that time customs were lax and many regarded recall from mourning as an honor, but Yue steadfastly declined and completed the full mourning period, winning great praise from discerning observers.

sentences.zh: 服終，復爲工部侍郎，俄拜兵部侍郎，加弘文館學士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he again became Vice Minister of Works, and before long was appointed Vice Minister of War and made a scholar of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he again became Vice Minister of Works, and before long was appointed Vice Minister of War and made a scholar of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，遷中書侍郎，兼雍州長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, Yue was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Chief Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Yue was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Chief Administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，譙王重福於東都構逆而死，留守捕系枝黨數百人，考訊結構之狀，經時不決。

translations.literal: In autumn Prince Qiao Chongfu plotted rebellion at the Eastern Capital and died; the regent arrested and imprisoned several hundred associates, interrogating the circumstances of the plot, but for a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Prince Qiao Chongfu plotted rebellion at the Eastern Capital and died. The regent arrested several hundred associates and interrogated them about the plot, but for a long time no verdict was reached.

sentences.zh: 睿宗令説往按其獄，一宿捕獲重福謀主張靈均、鄭愔等，盡得其情狀，自餘枉被繋禁者，一切釋放。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong ordered Yue to go investigate the case; in one night he captured Chongfu's chief plotters Zhang Lingjun, Zheng Yin, and others, fully obtaining the circumstances, and released all the rest who had been wrongly imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong sent Yue to investigate the case. In a single night he captured the chief plotters Zhang Lingjun and Zheng Yin and learned the full circumstances. All who had been wrongly imprisoned were released.

sentences.zh: 睿宗勞之曰：「知卿按此獄，不枉良善，又不漏罪人。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong commended him, saying, "I know that in investigating this case you did not wrong the good, nor did you let the guilty escape.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong commended him, saying, "In investigating this case you neither wronged the innocent nor let the guilty escape.

sentences.zh: 非卿忠正，豈能如此？

translations.literal: If not for your loyalty and uprightness, how could it have been thus?
translations.idiomatic: Without your loyalty and integrity, how could this have been done?

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，説與國子司業褚無量俱爲侍讀，深見親敬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, Yue together with Director of Studies Chu Wuliang both served as lecturers and were deeply treated with intimacy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong was crown prince, Yue and Director of Studies Chu Wuliang both served as his lecturers and were treated with deep affection and respect.

sentences.zh: 明年，同中書門下平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: The next year he received the title of Co-Drafter of the Secretariat and concurrently oversaw the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Co-Drafter of the Secretariat and was charged with overseeing the national history.

sentences.zh: 是歳二月，睿宗謂侍臣曰：「有術者上言，五日內有急兵入宮，卿等爲朕備之。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year Emperor Ruizong said to his attending ministers, "A practitioner of arts has reported that within five days urgent troops will enter the palace—you must prepare for this on my behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of that year Emperor Ruizong told his ministers, "A diviner has reported that within five days armed troops will enter the palace. You must prepare for this on my behalf.

sentences.zh: 」左右相顧莫能對，説進曰：「此是讒人設計，擬搖動東宮耳。

translations.literal: " Those to left and right looked at one another and none could reply; Yue advanced and said, "This is a slander's design, intended to shake the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Those around him looked at one another in silence. Yue stepped forward and said, "This is a slander's plot, intended to unsettle the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 陛下若使太子監國，則君臣分定，自然窺覦路絕，災難不生。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty has the crown prince oversee the state, then ruler and minister roles will be fixed, naturally the path of covetous ambition will be cut off, and disaster will not arise.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty has the crown prince oversee the state, the roles of ruler and minister will be fixed, ambition will have no opening, and disaster will not arise.

sentences.zh: 」睿宗大悅，即日下制皇太子監國。

translations.literal: " Emperor Ruizong was greatly pleased and that same day issued an order that the crown prince oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Ruizong was greatly pleased and that same day ordered the crown prince to oversee the state.

sentences.zh: 明年，又制皇太子即帝位。

translations.literal: The next year he also ordered the crown prince to ascend the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he ordered the crown prince to ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 俄而太平公主引蕭至忠、崔湜等爲宰相，以説爲不附己，轉爲尚書左丞，罷知政事，仍令往東都留司。

translations.literal: Before long Princess Taiping brought in Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi, and others as chief ministers; because Yue did not attach himself to her, he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, removed from managing affairs of state, and still ordered to remain at the Eastern Capital on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Princess Taiping installed Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi, and others as chief ministers. Because Yue would not attach himself to her, he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, removed from governance, and ordered to remain on duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 説既知太平等陰懷異計，乃因使獻佩刀於玄宗，請先事討之，玄宗深嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When Yue learned that Taiping and the others secretly harbored treacherous designs, he took advantage of an envoy to present a girdle knife to Emperor Xuanzong and requested to strike first; Emperor Xuanzong deeply approved and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue learned that Taiping and her faction secretly harbored treacherous designs, he sent a girdle knife to Emperor Xuanzong through an envoy and asked to strike first. Emperor Xuanzong deeply approved.

sentences.zh: 及至忠等伏誅，征拜中書令，封燕國公，賜實封二百戸。

translations.literal: When Zhizhong and the others were executed, Yue was summoned and appointed Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan state, and granted two hundred households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhizhong and the others were executed, Yue was summoned as Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan, and granted an actual income fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其冬，改易官名，拜紫微令。

translations.literal: That winter official titles were changed, and he was appointed Director of the Purple Micro Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when official titles were changed, he was appointed Director of the Purple Micro Palace.

sentences.zh: 自則天末年，季冬爲潑寒胡戲，中宗嘗御樓以觀之。

translations.literal: From the last years of Empress Wu, in late winter there was the Pot-Han barbarian play; Emperor Zhongzong once mounted the tower to watch it.
translations.idiomatic: From the last years of Empress Wu's reign, a Pot-Han barbarian play was performed in late winter. Emperor Zhongzong had once mounted the tower to watch it.

sentences.zh: 至是，因蕃夷入朝，又作此戲。

translations.literal: At this time, because foreign tribes came to court, the play was performed again.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, with foreign tribes coming to court, the play was performed again.

sentences.zh: 説上疏諫曰：「臣聞韓宣適魯，見周禮而嘆；

translations.literal: Yue submitted a remonstrance memorial saying, "Your subject has heard that when Han Xuan went to Lu he saw the rites of Zhou and sighed;
translations.idiomatic: Yue submitted a remonstrance memorial saying, "I have heard that when Han Xuan went to Lu he saw the rites of Zhou and sighed;

sentences.zh: 孔子會齊，數倡優之罪。

translations.literal: when Confucius met with Qi he repeatedly counted the offenses of performers.
translations.idiomatic: and when Confucius met with Qi he repeatedly condemned the offenses of performers.

sentences.zh: 列國如此，況天朝乎。

translations.literal: If the feudal states were thus, how much more the heavenly court!
translations.idiomatic: If even the feudal states held such standards, how much more should the imperial court!

sentences.zh: 今外蕃請和，選使朝謁，所望接以禮樂，示以兵威。

translations.literal: Now the outer tribes seek peace and envoys are chosen to attend court; what is hoped is to receive them with rites and music and display military might.
translations.idiomatic: Now foreign tribes seek peace and envoys have come to court. We should receive them with rites and music and display our military might.

sentences.zh: 雖曰戎夷，不可輕易，焉知無駒支之辯，由餘之賢哉？

translations.literal: Though they are called barbarians, they must not be treated lightly—who knows whether there may not be another Juzhi in eloquence or another Youyu in talent?
translations.idiomatic: Though they are called barbarians, they must not be treated lightly. Who knows whether among them there may not be another Juzhi in eloquence or another Youyu in talent?

sentences.zh: 且潑寒胡未聞典故，裸體跳足，盛德何觀；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Pot-Han play is not found in classical precedent; naked bodies and bare feet—what great virtue is there to behold?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Pot-Han play has no precedent in the classics. Naked bodies and bare feet—what virtue is there to display?

sentences.zh: 揮水投泥，失容斯甚。

translations.literal: Splashing water and throwing mud—how extremely unseemly!
translations.idiomatic: Splashing water and throwing mud—how utterly unseemly!

sentences.zh: 法殊魯禮，褻比齊優，恐非幹羽柔遠之義，樽俎折沖之禮。

translations.literal: Its methods differ from the rites of Lu and are as unseemly as the performers of Qi; I fear this is not the principle of winning the distant through shields and feathers, nor the rite of breaking the enemy's will at the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs differ from the rites of Lu and are as unseemly as the performers of Qi. I fear this is not the principle of winning the distant through civil virtue, nor the rite of defeating the enemy at the banquet table.

sentences.zh: 」自是此戲乃絕。

translations.literal: " From this the play was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time the play was abolished.

sentences.zh: 俄而爲姚崇所構，出爲相州刺史，仍充河北道按察使。

translations.literal: Before long he was framed by Yao Chong and sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou, still serving as inspector of the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was framed by Yao Chong and sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou while also serving as inspector of the Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 俄又坐事左轉岳州刺史，仍停所食實封三百戸，遷右羽林將軍，兼檢校幽州都督。

translations.literal: Before long he was again demoted for an offense to prefect of Yuezhou, had three hundred households of his actual fief income suspended, was transferred to General of the Right Feathered Forest, and concurrently made acting military governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted for an offense to prefect of Yuezhou, had three hundred households of his actual fief income suspended, was made General of the Right Feathered Forest, and concurrently acting military governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: ，檢校并州大都督府長史，兼天兵軍大使，攝御史大夫，兼修國史，仍賫史本隨軍修撰。

translations.literal: He was made acting Chief Administrator of the Bingzhou Metropolitan Area Command, concurrently envoy of the Tianbing Army, acting Censor-in-Chief, and concurrently compiler of the national history, still carrying the draft history with the army to continue compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Chief Administrator of the Bingzhou Metropolitan Area Command, concurrently envoy of the Tianbing Army, acting Censor-in-Chief, and compiler of the national history, carrying the draft history with the army to continue his work.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，朔方大使王晙誅河曲降虜阿布思等千餘人。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year the Shuofang envoy Wang Jun executed more than a thousand surrendered captives of the river bend, including Abu Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year the Shuofang envoy Wang Jun executed more than a thousand surrendered tribesmen of the river bend, including Abu Si.

sentences.zh: 時并州大同、橫野等軍有九姓同羅、拔曳固等部落，皆懷震懼。

translations.literal: At that time at Datong, Hengye, and other armies of Bingzhou there were tribes of the Nine Surnames, Tongluo, Bayegu, and others, all filled with shock and fear.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Datong, Hengye, and other armies of Bingzhou included tribes of the Nine Surnames, Tongluo, Bayegu, and others, all of whom were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 説率輕騎二十人，持旌節直詣其部落，宿於帳下，召酋帥以慰撫之。

translations.literal: Yue led twenty light cavalry, bearing credentials went straight to their tribes, lodged beneath their tents, and summoned the chieftains to comfort and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue led twenty light cavalry, went straight to their tribes bearing credentials, lodged in their tents, and summoned the chieftains to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 副使李憲以爲夷虜難信，不宜輕涉不測，馳狀以諫，説報書曰：「吾肉非黃羊，必不畏吃；

translations.literal: The deputy envoy Li Xian believed that barbarians are hard to trust and that one should not lightly venture into the unpredictable. He sent a dispatch to remonstrate. Yue replied in a letter, saying, "My flesh is not that of a yellow sheep—I surely do not fear being eaten;
translations.idiomatic: The deputy envoy Li Xian believed that barbarians could not be trusted and that one should not lightly venture into uncertainty. He sent an urgent dispatch to remonstrate. Yue replied in a letter: "My flesh is not that of a yellow sheep—I have no fear of being eaten;

sentences.zh: 血非野馬，必不畏刺。

translations.literal: My blood is not that of a wild horse—I surely do not fear being pierced.
translations.idiomatic: My blood is not that of a wild horse—I have no fear of being slashed.

sentences.zh: 士見危致命，是吾效死之秋也。

translations.literal: When a gentleman sees danger he gives his life—this is the season in which I shall die in service.
translations.idiomatic: When a gentleman faces danger, he lays down his life—this is my moment to die in service.

sentences.zh: 」於是九姓感義，其心乃安。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Nine Surnames were moved by his righteousness, and their hearts were put at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Nine Surnames were moved by his loyalty, and their hearts were reassured.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，胡賊康待賓率眾反，據長泉縣，自稱葉護，攻陷蘭池等六州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year the Hu bandit Kang Daibin led troops in rebellion, seized Changquan County, styled himself Yehu, and captured six prefectures including Lanchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year the Hu rebel Kang Daibin rose in rebellion, seized Changquan County, styled himself Yehu, and captured six prefectures including Lanchi.

sentences.zh: 詔王晙率兵討之，仍令説相知經略。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wang Jun to lead troops against him, and Yue was also made to direct overall strategy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Jun to lead troops against him and placed Yue in charge of overall strategy.

sentences.zh: 時叛胡與党項連結，攻銀城、連谷，以據倉糧，説統馬步萬人出合河關掩擊，大破之。

translations.literal: At that time the rebellious Hu joined with the Tangut tribes, attacked Yincheng and Liangu, and seized the granary stores. Yue commanded ten thousand cavalry and infantry and went out through Hehe Pass to strike by surprise, crushing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebel Hu allied with the Tangut tribes, attacked Yincheng and Liangu to seize the granary stores. Yue commanded ten thousand cavalry and infantry through Hehe Pass in a surprise attack and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 追至駱駝堰，胡及党項自相殺。

translations.literal: Pursuing them to Luotuo Dam, the Hu and Tangut turned on one another and killed each other.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to Luotuo Dam, the Hu and Tangut turned on one another in mutual slaughter.

sentences.zh: 阻夜，胡乃西遁入鐵建山，餘黨潰散。

translations.literal: Blocked by night, the Hu fled west into Mount Tiejian and the remaining bands scattered in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked by nightfall, the Hu fled west into Mount Tiejian, and the remaining bands scattered in defeat.

sentences.zh: 説招集党項，復其居業。

translations.literal: Yue summoned and gathered the Tangut, restoring them to their dwellings and occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Yue gathered the Tangut people and restored them to their homes and livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 副使史獻請因此誅党項，絕其翻動之計，説曰：「先王之道，推亡固存，如盡誅之，是逆天道也。

translations.literal: The deputy envoy Shi Xian asked that the Tangut be executed on this occasion to cut off their scheme of turning traitor.
