Yue said, "The Way of the former kings was to push toward extinction what is perishing and strengthen what remains. If we kill them all, we would be going against Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy envoy Shi Xian proposed executing the Tangut to prevent them from rebelling. Yue said, "The Way of the former kings was to allow the doomed to perish and strengthen what still endured. To kill them all would be to defy Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 」因奏置麟州，以安置党項餘燼。

translations.literal: " He then memorialized to establish Lin Prefecture to resettle the remaining embers of the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: " He then memorialized for the establishment of Lin Prefecture to resettle the surviving Tangut.

sentences.zh: 其年，拜兵部尚書、同中書門下三品，仍依舊修國史。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Minister of War and Third Rank at the Chancellery and Secretariat, still continuing to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed Minister of War and Third Rank at the Chancellery and Secretariat, while continuing to compile the national history as before.

sentences.zh: 明年，又敕説爲朔方軍節度大使，往巡五城，處置兵馬。

translations.literal: The next year an edict again made Yue military governor of the Shuofang Army and sent him to inspect the Five Cities and manage troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yue was again appointed military governor of the Shuofang Army and sent to inspect the Five Cities and manage the disposition of troops.

sentences.zh: 時有康待賓餘黨慶州方渠降胡康願子自立爲可汗，舉兵反，謀掠監牧馬，西涉河出塞。

translations.literal: At that time a remnant of Kang Daibin's followers—Kang Yuanzi, a surrendered Hu of Fangqu in Qing Prefecture—declared himself khan, raised troops in rebellion, plotted to seize the imperial stud horses, and planned to cross the Yellow River westward and leave the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kang Yuanzi, a remnant follower of Kang Daibin and a surrendered Hu of Fangqu in Qing Prefecture, declared himself khan, rebelled, plotted to seize the imperial stud horses, and intended to cross the Yellow River westward and flee beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 説進兵討擒之，並獲其家屬於木盤山，送都斬之，其黨悉平，獲男女三千餘人。

translations.literal: Yue advanced with troops, captured him, also seized his family at Mount Mupan, sent them to the capital for execution, pacified his followers entirely, and captured more than three thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Yue advanced, captured him, and also seized his family at Mount Mupan. He sent them to the capital for execution, fully pacified the rebel band, and took more than three thousand captives, men and women.

sentences.zh: 於是移河曲六州殘胡五萬餘口配許、汝、唐、鄧、仙、豫等州，始空河南逆方千里之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than fifty thousand remnant Hu from the six prefectures of the river bend were relocated and assigned to Xu, Ru, Tang, Deng, Xian, Yu, and other prefectures, beginning to empty the thousand-li region of the rebellious south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon more than fifty thousand remnant Hu from the six prefectures of the river bend were relocated to Xu, Ru, Tang, Deng, Xian, Yu, and other prefectures, finally clearing the thousand-li stretch of rebellious territory south of the river.

sentences.zh: 説以討賊功，復賜實封二百戸。

translations.literal: For his merit in suppressing the bandits, Yue was again granted two hundred households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in suppressing the rebels, Yue was again granted an actual income fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 先是，緣邊鎮兵常六十餘萬，説以時無強寇，不假師眾，奏罷二十餘萬，勒還營農。

translations.literal: Previously, frontier garrison troops had commonly totaled more than six hundred thousand. Yue, because there were no powerful enemies at the time and great forces were not needed, memorialized to dismiss more than two hundred thousand and ordered them back to garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: Previously frontier garrison troops had numbered more than six hundred thousand. Yue argued that with no strong enemy at hand there was no need for so large a host, and memorialized to dismiss more than two hundred thousand troops and return them to garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 玄宗頗以爲疑，説奏曰：「臣久在疆場，具悉邊事，軍將但欲自衞及雜使營私。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was quite doubtful about this. Yue memorialized, saying, "Your servant has long been on the frontier and knows border affairs thoroughly. Military commanders only wish to defend themselves and use miscellaneous laborers for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was quite skeptical. Yue memorialized: "I have long served on the frontier and know border affairs thoroughly. Military commanders care only about protecting themselves and using subordinates for private profit.

sentences.zh: 若禦敵制勝，不在多擁閑冗，以妨農務。

translations.literal: To repel enemies and achieve victory does not depend on maintaining idle and redundant troops to the detriment of agricultural work.
translations.idiomatic: Victory over the enemy does not require maintaining idle hordes of troops at the expense of farming.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以爲疑，臣請以闔門百口爲保。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty still has doubts, I ask to pledge the hundred mouths of my household as guarantee.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty still has doubts, I pledge the lives of my entire household as guarantee.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之明，四夷畏伏，必不慮減兵而招寇也。

translations.literal: Given Your Majesty's brilliance, the Four Barbarians cower in submission—they will surely not fear that reducing troops will invite invaders."
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's wisdom, the Four Barbarians submit in awe—there is no danger that reducing the army will invite invasion."

sentences.zh: 」上乃從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor then assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 時當番衞士，浸以貧弱，逃亡略盡。

translations.literal: At that time the rotating palace guards had gradually become poor and weak, and desertions were nearly total.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rotating palace guards had grown progressively poorer and weaker, and deserters were nearly all gone.

sentences.zh: 説又建策，請一切罷之，別召募強壯，令其宿衞，不簡色役，優爲條例，逋逃者必爭來應募。

translations.literal: Yue also proposed a plan: to abolish them entirely, separately recruit strong men to serve as night guards, not screen by corvée status, and grant favorable regulations, so that fugitives would surely compete to come forward for enlistment.
translations.idiomatic: Yue also proposed abolishing the old system entirely and instead recruiting able-bodied men for garrison duty, without screening by corvée status and with favorable regulations, so that fugitives would compete to enlist.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 旬日，得精兵一十三萬人，分系諸衞，更番上下，以實京師，其後彍騎是也。

translations.literal: Within ten days he obtained one hundred and thirty thousand elite troops, assigned them to the various guards, rotated them up and down in shifts, and thus reinforced the capital—this was the origin of the Kuoriders.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he raised one hundred and thirty thousand elite troops, assigned them to the various guard corps on rotating shifts to reinforce the capital. This was the origin of the Kuoriders.

sentences.zh: 是歳，玄宗將還京，而便幸并州，説進言曰：「太原是國家王業所起，陛下行幸，振威耀武，並建碑紀德，以申永思之意。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Xuanzong was about to return to the capital but intended to visit Bingzhou on the way. Yue submitted advice, saying, "Taiyuan is where the imperial enterprise of our state began. When Your Majesty visits there, displaying majesty and shining with martial glory, you should also erect a stele to record virtue and express your enduring remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor planned to return to the capital but also to visit Bingzhou en route. Yue submitted advice: "Taiyuan is where the dynasty's royal enterprise began. When Your Majesty tours there, displaying majesty and martial splendor, you should also erect a stele to commemorate its virtue and express your enduring gratitude.

sentences.zh: 若便入京，路由河東，有漢武脽上後土之祀，此禮久闕，歷代莫能行之。

translations.literal: If you then proceed to the capital, the route passes through Hedong, where there was Emperor Wu of Han's sacrifice to Houtu at Shimao. This rite has long been neglected—no dynasty has been able to perform it.
translations.idiomatic: If you then proceed to the capital, the route passes through Hedong, where Emperor Wu of Han once offered sacrifice to Houtu at Shimao. That rite has long been abandoned, and no dynasty since has been able to perform it.

sentences.zh: 願陛下紹斯墜典，以爲三農祈谷，此誠萬姓之福也。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would revive this fallen rite to pray for grain on behalf of the three classes of farmers—this would truly be a blessing for the myriad people."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to revive this fallen rite and offer sacrifice for the harvest on behalf of the farmers—it would be a true blessing for the common people."

sentences.zh: 」上從其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 及祀後土禮畢，説代張嘉貞爲中書令。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice to Houtu was completed, Yue replaced Zhang Jiazhen as Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice to Houtu was completed, Yue replaced Zhang Jiazhen as Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，玄宗親爲詔曰：「動惟直道，累聞獻替之誠；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Emperor Xuanzong personally composed an edict, saying, "In conduct he holds only to the upright Way; I have repeatedly heard his sincere counsel for improvement;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the emperor personally composed an edict: "In conduct he holds steadfastly to the upright Way; I have repeatedly heard his sincere counsel for improvement;

sentences.zh: 言則不諛，自得謀猷之體。

translations.literal: in speech he does not flatter, naturally possessing the substance of strategic counsel.
translations.idiomatic: in speech he never flatters, naturally possessing the substance of true counsel.

sentences.zh: 政令必俟其增損，圖書又藉其刊削，才望兼著，理合褒升。

translations.literal: Government orders await his additions and deletions; books and records rely on his editing and pruning. Talent and reputation are both outstanding—promotion is only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Government orders await his revisions; books and records depend on his editing. Both talent and reputation are distinguished—promotion is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 考中上。

translations.literal: His evaluation: upper-middle.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation: upper-middle.

sentences.zh: 説又首建封禪之議。

translations.literal: Yue was also the first to propose the fengshan ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was also the first to propose the feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 十三年，受詔與右散騎常侍徐堅、太常少卿韋縚等撰東封儀註。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he received an edict to compile the rites and regulations for the eastern fengshan together with Right Regular Attendant Xu Jian, Vice Minister of Rites Wei Shao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to compile the ritual regulations for the eastern fengshan together with Right Regular Attendant Xu Jian, Vice Minister of Rites Wei Shao, and others.

sentences.zh: 舊儀不便者，説多所裁正，語在《禮志》。

translations.literal: Where the old rites were inconvenient, Yue made many corrections; the details are in the Rites Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Where the old rites proved inadequate, Yue made numerous corrections; details are recorded in the Rites Treatise.

sentences.zh: 玄宗尋召説及禮官學士等賜宴於集仙殿，謂説曰：「今與卿等賢才同宴於此，宜改名爲集賢殿。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Xuanzong summoned Yue, ritual officials, academicians, and others to a banquet in the Hall of Assembled Immortals. He said to Yue, "Now that I banquet here with you and other men of talent, it should be renamed the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor summoned Yue, ritual officials, and academicians to a banquet in the Hall of Assembled Immortals and said to Yue, "Now that I feast here with you and other men of talent, this hall should be renamed the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 」因下制改麗正書院爲集賢殿書院，授説集賢院學士，知院事。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued changing the Lizheng Academy into the Academy of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. Yue was appointed Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies and put in charge of its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict was then issued renaming the Lizheng Academy as the Academy of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. Yue was appointed Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies and placed in charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 及將東封，授説爲右丞相兼中書令，源乾曜爲左丞相兼侍中，蓋勒成岱宗，以明宰相佐成王化也。

translations.literal: When the eastern fengshan was about to take place, Yue was made Right Counselor and concurrent Director of the Chancellery, and Yuan Qianyao was made Left Counselor and concurrent Palace Counselor—intended to inscribe achievement on Mount Tai and make clear that the chief ministers assist in completing royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern fengshan was imminent, Yue was made Right Counselor and concurrent Director of the Chancellery, and Yuan Qianyao was made Left Counselor and concurrent Palace Counselor—symbolically inscribing achievement on Mount Tai to show that the chief ministers assist in the kingly transformation.

sentences.zh: 説又撰《封禪壇頌》以紀聖德。

translations.literal: Yue also composed "Ode to the Fengshan Altar" to commemorate the sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue also composed the "Ode to the Fengshan Altar" to commemorate imperial virtue.

sentences.zh: 初，源乾曜本意不欲封禪，而説因贊其事，由是頗不相平。

translations.literal: Originally Yuan Qianyao had not wished to conduct the fengshan, but Yue supported the undertaking, and for this reason they were quite at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao had originally opposed the fengshan, but Yue supported it, and for this reason the two were quite at odds.

sentences.zh: 及登山，説引所親攝供奉官及主事等從升，加階超入五品，其餘官多不得上。

translations.literal: When ascending the mountain, Yue brought his close associates—acting supply officers and clerks—to accompany him up, promoted them by rank into the fifth grade, while most other officials could not ascend.
translations.idiomatic: When ascending the mountain, Yue brought his personal associates—acting supply officers and clerks—to accompany him, promoting them by rank into the fifth grade, while most other officials were denied ascent.

sentences.zh: 又行從兵士，惟加勛，不得賜物，由是頗爲內外所怨。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the soldiers in the procession received only honors and no gifts of goods, and for this reason he was much resented inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the soldiers in the procession received only honors and no gifts, for which he was much resented at court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 先是，御史中丞宇文融獻策，請括天下逃戸及籍外剩田，置十道勸農使，分往檢察。

translations.literal: Earlier, Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong had submitted a plan to register all fugitive households and surplus fields outside the tax rolls throughout the empire, establish ten Agricultural Encouragement Commissioners, and dispatch them to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong had proposed registering all fugitive households and surplus fields outside the tax rolls empire-wide, establishing ten Agricultural Encouragement Commissioners, and dispatching them to conduct inspections.

sentences.zh: 説嫌其擾人不便，數建議違之。

translations.literal: Yue disliked how it troubled the people and was inconvenient, and repeatedly submitted proposals in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Yue considered it disruptive and repeatedly submitted memorials in opposition.

sentences.zh: 及東封還，融又密奏分吏部置十銓，融與禮部尚書蘇颋等分掌選事。

translations.literal: After returning from the eastern fengshan, Rong again secretly memorialized to divide the Ministry of Personnel into ten boards. Rong and Minister of Rites Su Ting and others separately managed selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the eastern fengshan, Rong secretly memorialized to divide the Ministry of Personnel into ten selection boards, with Rong, Minister of Rites Su Ting, and others each managing appointments.

sentences.zh: 融等每有奏請，皆爲説所抑，由是銓綜失敘。

translations.literal: Whenever Rong and the others submitted requests, Yue blocked them, and for this reason appointments fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Rong and his faction submitted requests, Yue blocked them, throwing the appointment process into disorder.

sentences.zh: 融乃與御史大夫崔隱甫、中丞李林甫奏彈説引術士夜解及受贓等狀，敕宰臣源乾曜、刑部尚書韋抗、大理少卿胡珪、御史大夫崔隱甫就尚書省鞫問。

translations.literal: Rong then joined Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinpu and Vice Censor Li Linfu in impeaching Yue for employing shamans, divination by night, accepting bribes, and the like. An edict ordered Chief Minister Yuan Qianyao, Minister of Justice Wei Kang, Vice Minister of Justice Hu Gui, and Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinpu to interrogate him at the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then joined with Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinpu and Vice Censor Li Linfu in impeaching Yue for consulting shamans, divining by night, and accepting bribes. An edict ordered Chief Minister Yuan Qianyao, Minister of Justice Wei Kang, Vice Minister of Justice Hu Gui, and Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinpu to interrogate him at the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 説兄左庶子光詣朝堂割耳稱冤。

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother, Left Sub-Prefect of the Crown Prince's Household Guang, went to the court hall, cut off his ear, and proclaimed his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's elder brother Guang, Left Sub-Prefect of the Crown Prince's Household, went to the court hall, cut off his ear, and pleaded his brother's innocence.

sentences.zh: 時中書主事張觀、左衞長史範堯臣並依倚説勢，詐假納賂，又私度僧王慶則往來與説占卜吉兇，爲隱甫等所鞫伏罪。

translations.literal: At that time Chancellery Clerk Zhang Guan and Left Guard Commandant Fan Yaochén both relied on Yue's power to commit fraud, accept bribes, and forge credentials. Also the private ordained monk Wang Qingze came and went with Yue to divine fortune and misfortune. All were interrogated by Yinpu and others and confessed to their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chancellery Clerk Zhang Guan and Left Guard Commandant Fan Yaochén had exploited Yue's power to accept bribes and issue fraudulent credentials. The privately ordained monk Wang Qingze also came and went with Yue to divination sessions. All were interrogated by Yinpu and confessed.

sentences.zh: 説經兩宿，玄宗使中官高力士視之，回奏：「説坐於草上，於瓦器中食，蓬首垢面，自罰憂懼之甚。

translations.literal: After two nights of interrogation, Emperor Xuanzong sent the eunuch Gao Lishi to observe him. He reported back: "Yue sits on grass, eats from earthenware vessels, his hair uncombed and face filthy, punishing himself in the utmost grief and fear.
translations.idiomatic: After two nights of interrogation, the emperor sent the eunuch Gao Lishi to observe him. He reported back: "Yue sits on a mat of straw, eats from earthenware bowls, his hair unkempt and face grimy, punishing himself in the utmost grief and fear.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗憫之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanzong took pity on him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took pity on him.

sentences.zh: 力士奏曰：「説曾爲侍讀，又於國有功。

translations.literal: Lishi memorialized, saying, "Yue once served as lecturer-in-waiting and has rendered merit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi memorialized: "Yue once served as lecturer-in-waiting and has rendered great service to the state.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗然其奏，由是停兼中書令，觀及慶則決杖而死，連坐遷貶者十餘人。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanzong approved his memorial. Thereupon Yue was removed from his concurrent post as Director of the Chancellery. Guan and Qingze were beaten to death with the rod, and more than ten others connected with the case were demoted and banished.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved. Yue was removed from his concurrent post as Director of the Chancellery. Guan and Qingze were beaten to death, and more than ten others implicated in the case were demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 隱甫及融等恐説復用爲己患，又密奏毀之。

translations.literal: Yinpu and Rong and the others feared that if Yue were restored to office he would be a threat to them, and again submitted secret memorials to slander him.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu, Rong, and their faction feared that if Yue were restored to power he would threaten them, and submitted secret memorials to denigrate him further.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔説致仕，仍令在家修史。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered Yue to retire, while still instructing him to compile history at home.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict ordered Yue to retire, while still directing him to compile history at home.

sentences.zh: 初，説爲相時，玄宗意欲討吐蕃，説密奏許其通和，以息邊境，玄宗不從。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yue was chief minister, Emperor Xuanzong intended to campaign against Tibet. Yue secretly memorialized to allow peace with them and quiet the frontier, but the emperor did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was chief minister, the emperor planned to campaign against Tibet. Yue secretly memorialized proposing peace to quiet the frontier, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 及瓜州失守，王掞死，説因獲巂州鬥羊，上表獻之，以申諷諭。

translations.literal: When Guazhou fell and Wang Han died, Yue obtained a fighting ram from Yizhou and submitted a memorial presenting it, to deliver an oblique admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When Guazhou fell and Wang Han was killed, Yue obtained a fighting ram from Yizhou and submitted a memorial presenting it as an oblique admonition.

sentences.zh: 其表：「臣聞勇士冠雞，武夫戴鹖，推情舉類，獲此鬥羊。

translations.literal: The memorial read: "Your servant has heard that brave warriors cap themselves with roosters and martial men wear the headdress of the crested myna. Extending by sentiment to similar things, I have obtained this fighting ram.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial read: "Your servant has heard that brave warriors wear roosters on their caps and martial men don the headdress of the crested myna. Following this principle of likeness, I have obtained this fighting ram.

sentences.zh: 遠生越巂，蓄性剛決，敵不避強，戰不顧死，雖爲微物，誌不可挫。

translations.literal: Born far away in Yuexi, it stores a nature of firm resolve, does not avoid strong foes in combat, does not regard death in battle. Though a small creature, its will cannot be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Born far away in Yuexi, it possesses a fierce and resolute nature—it does not shrink from strong foes, it does not flinch from death in battle. Though a small creature, its spirit cannot be broken.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下選良家於六郡，求猛士於四方，鳥不遁才，獸不藏伎。

translations.literal: Humbly considering that Your Majesty selects good families from the Six Commanderies and seeks fierce warriors from the four directions—no bird conceals its talent, no beast hides its skill.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considering that Your Majesty selects good families from the Six Commanderies and seeks fierce warriors from the four directions—no bird hides its talent, no beast conceals its skill.

sentences.zh: 如蒙效奇靈圃，角力天場，卻鼓怒以作氣，前躑躅以奮擊。

translations.literal: If it may be allowed to display its marvel in the spirit garden and test strength in the heavenly arena, it rears back in fury to gather its spirit and advances in stamping fury to strike with might.
translations.idiomatic: Were it permitted to display its marvel in the imperial garden and contest strength in the heavenly arena, it would rear back in fury to gather its spirit and advance stamping to strike with all its might.

sentences.zh: 趹若奔雲之交觸，碎如轉石之相叩，裂骨賭勝，濺血爭雄，敢毅見而沖冠，鷙狠聞而擊節。

translations.literal: Their clashes like rushing clouds meeting, their shattering like rolling stones striking—the staking of bones for victory, the splashing of blood contending for supremacy would make the bold and resolute flush with rage and the fierce and cruel beat time in approval.
translations.idiomatic: Their clashes would be like rushing clouds colliding, their impacts like rolling stones striking together—staking bones for victory, splashing blood in contest for supremacy—enough to make the bold flush with rage and the fierce beat their hands in approval.

sentences.zh: 冀將少助明主市駿骨、揖怒蛙之意也。

translations.literal: I hope this may slightly assist the enlightened lord's intent of buying the steed's bones and bowing to the angry frog."
translations.idiomatic: I hope this may in some small measure echo the enlightened lord's purpose in buying the steed's bones and bowing to the angry frog."

sentences.zh: 若使羊能言，必將曰『若鬥不解，立有死者』。

translations.literal: If the ram could speak, it would surely say, 'If the fight does not end, death will immediately follow.'
translations.idiomatic: Were the ram able to speak, it would surely say, 'If the fight does not stop, death will follow at once.'

sentences.zh: 所賴至仁無殘，量力取勸焉。

translations.literal: What relies on it is the utmost benevolence without cruelty—measuring strength to offer admonition.
translations.idiomatic: It depends on the utmost benevolence without cruelty—measuring one's strength before offering counsel.

sentences.zh: 臣緣損足，未堪履地，謹遣男詣金明門奉進。

translations.literal: Your servant, because of an injured foot, cannot yet tread the ground, and respectfully sends my son to present it at the Jinming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, having injured his foot, cannot yet walk, and respectfully sends his son to present it at the Jinming Gate.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗深悟其意，賜絹及雜彩一千匹。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanzong deeply grasped his meaning and granted him one thousand bolts of silk and miscellaneous colored fabrics.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor deeply grasped his meaning and granted him one thousand bolts of silk and colored fabrics.

sentences.zh: 十七年，復拜尚書左丞相、集賢院學士，尋代源乾曜爲尚書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was again appointed Left Counselor of the Ministry of State Affairs and Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, and soon replaced Yuan Qianyao as Left Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was again appointed Left Counselor of the Ministry of State Affairs and Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, soon replacing Yuan Qianyao as Left Counselor.

sentences.zh: 視事之日，上敕所司供帳，設音樂，內出酒食，御制詩一篇以敘其事。

translations.literal: On the day he assumed office, the emperor ordered the relevant offices to provide supplies and pavilions, arranged music, sent out wine and food from the inner palace, and composed an imperial poem to relate the affair.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he assumed office, the emperor ordered provisions and pavilions arranged, music performed, wine and food sent from the inner palace, and composed an imperial poem to commemorate the occasion.

sentences.zh: 尋以修謁陵儀註功，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Before long, for his merit in compiling the rites for visiting the imperial tombs, he was given the additional title of Grand Master of Glorious Affairs with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was given the additional title of Grand Master of Glorious Affairs with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies for his work compiling the rites for visiting the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 時長子均爲中書舍人，次子垍尚寧親公主，拜駙馬都尉，又特授説兄慶王傅光爲銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At that time his eldest son Jun was Attendant Drafting at the Chancellery; his second son Jiao married Princess Ningqin and was appointed Captain of the Feathered Forest; and his brother Guang, Tutor of the Prince of Qing, was specially granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his eldest son Jun served as Attendant Drafting at the Chancellery; his second son Jiao married Princess Ningqin and was appointed Captain of the Feathered Forest; and Yue's brother Guang, Tutor of the Prince of Qing, was specially granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 當時榮寵，莫與爲比。

translations.literal: The honors and favor of that time had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: No one of the time could match his honors and favor.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遇疾，玄宗每日令中使問疾，並手寫藥方賜之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he fell ill. Each day Emperor Xuanzong sent palace eunuchs to inquire after his health and personally wrote out prescriptions to grant him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he fell ill. Each day the emperor sent palace eunuchs to inquire after his health and personally wrote out prescriptions for him.

sentences.zh: 十二月薨，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died; he was sixty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 上慘惻久之，遽於光順門舉哀，因罷十九年元正朝會，詔曰：

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply grieved for a long while, hastened to perform mourning rites at the Guangshun Gate, and for this reason canceled the New Year's court assembly of the nineteenth year. An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply for a long time, hastened to perform mourning rites at the Guangshun Gate, and canceled the New Year's court assembly of the nineteenth year. An edict read:

sentences.zh: 始玄宗在東宮，説已蒙禮遇。

translations.literal: From the beginning when Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, Yue had already received courteous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the emperor was crown prince, Yue had already enjoyed his favor.

sentences.zh: 及太平用事，儲位頗危，説獨排其黨，請太子監國，深謀密畫，竟清內難，遂爲開元宗臣。

translations.literal: When Princess Taiping held power and the heir's position was quite perilous, Yue alone opposed her faction, petitioned that the crown prince supervise the state, and through deep planning and secret scheming finally cleared the internal crisis, becoming thereafter a founding minister of the Kaiyuan reign.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Taiping held power and the heir's position grew perilous, Yue alone opposed her faction, petitioned for the crown prince to supervise the state, and through deep planning and secret counsel finally resolved the internal crisis, becoming a founding minister of the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 前後三秉大政，掌文學之任凡三十年。

translations.literal: Before and after, he thrice held great governance and managed literary affairs for thirty years in all.
translations.idiomatic: He thrice held the highest governance and directed literary affairs for thirty years in all.

sentences.zh: 爲文俊麗，用思精密，朝廷大手筆，皆特承中旨撰述，天下詞人，咸諷誦之。

translations.literal: His writing was brilliant and elegant, his thought refined and meticulous. All the court's grand compositions were specially composed on imperial order under his hand, and literary men throughout the realm recited them.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was brilliant and elegant, his thought refined and meticulous. The court's major compositions were all composed at special imperial command under his hand, and poets throughout the realm recited them.

sentences.zh: 尤長於碑文、墓誌，當代無能及者。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at stele inscriptions and tomb epitaphs—no one of his time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled especially at stele inscriptions and tomb epitaphs—no contemporary could match him.

sentences.zh: 喜延納後進，善用己長，引文儒之士，佐佑王化，當承平歳久，誌在粉飾盛時。

translations.literal: He delighted in receiving and nurturing juniors, making good use of his own strengths, drawing in literary scholars to assist royal transformation. In long years of peace, his ambition was to adorn the flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in nurturing younger scholars, making good use of his talents, and drawing in literary men to assist the kingly transformation. In those long years of peace, his ambition was to adorn the flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 其封泰山，祠脽上，謁五陵，開集賢，修太宗之政，皆説爲倡首。

translations.literal: His feng on Mount Tai, sacrifice at Shimao, visit to the Five Tombs, founding of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, and restoration of Emperor Taizong's policies—all were led by Yue as initiator.
translations.idiomatic: The feng on Mount Tai, the sacrifice at Shimao, the visit to the Five Tombs, the founding of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, and the restoration of Emperor Taizong's policies—all were initiatives that Yue led.

sentences.zh: 而又敦氣義，重然諾，於君臣朋友之際，大義甚篤。

translations.literal: Moreover he cherished integrity and honor, valued promises kept—in relations between ruler and subject and among friends, his devotion to righteousness was profound.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he cherished integrity and valued his promises—in relations between ruler and subject and among friends, his devotion to righteousness was profound.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人徐堅自負文學，常以集賢院學士多非其人，所司供膳太厚，嘗謂朝列曰：「此輩於國家何益，如此虛費。

translations.literal: At that time Attendant Drafting Xu Jian, proud of his literary achievement, often said that many academicians at the Academy of Assembled Worthies were unworthy men and that the provisions supplied them were too lavish. He once said to the court ranks, "What use are these people to the state? Such wasteful expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Attendant Drafting Xu Jian, proud of his literary ability, often complained that many academicians at the Academy of Assembled Worthies were unworthy and that their provisions were too lavish. He once said to the court assembly: "What use are these people to the state? Such wasteful expenditure.

sentences.zh: 」將建議罷之。

translations.literal: " He was about to propose abolishing it.
translations.idiomatic: " He was about to propose abolishing the academy.

sentences.zh: 説曰：「自古帝王功成，則有奢縱之失，或興池臺，或玩聲色。

translations.literal: Yue said, "Since ancient times when emperors achieved success they fell into extravagance—some built ponds and terraces, some indulged in music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said: "Since ancient times, when emperors achieved success they fell into extravagance—some built ponds and terraces, others indulged in music and women.

sentences.zh: 今聖上崇儒重道，親自講論，刊正圖書，詳延學者。

translations.literal: Now the sage emperor honors Confucianism and esteems the Way, personally lecturing and discussing, correcting and editing books, and extensively recruiting scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sage emperor honors Confucianism and esteems the Way, personally lecturing, correcting books, and extensively recruiting scholars.

sentences.zh: 今麗正書院，天子禮樂之司，永代規模，不易之道也。

translations.literal: Now the Lizheng Academy is the office of the Son of Heaven's rites and music—a model for all ages, an unchanging Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Lizheng Academy is the Son of Heaven's office of rites and music—a model for all ages and an unchanging institution.

sentences.zh: 所費者細，所益者大。

translations.literal: What is spent is small; what is gained is great.
translations.idiomatic: The cost is small; the benefit is great.

sentences.zh: 徐子之言，何其隘哉！

translations.literal: Master Xu's words—how narrow-minded!
translations.idiomatic: Master Xu's words—how narrow-minded!

sentences.zh: 」玄宗知之，由是薄堅。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Xuanzong learned of this, he thereupon regarded Xu Jian with disfavor.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor learned of this, he came to regard Xu Jian with disfavor.

sentences.zh: 説既遭訕鑠，罷知政事，專集賢文史之任，每軍國大事，帝遣中使先訪其可否。

translations.literal: After Yue suffered slander and calumny and was removed from governance, he devoted himself solely to the Academy's literary and historical duties. For every major military or state affair, the emperor sent palace eunuchs first to ask his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue suffered slander and was removed from governance, he devoted himself to the Academy's literary and historical duties. For every major military or state matter, the emperor sent palace eunuchs first to consult him.

sentences.zh: 説嘗自制其父《贈丹州刺史騭碑文》，玄宗聞之而御書其碑額賜之曰「嗚呼，積善之墓」。

translations.literal: Yue once personally composed the stele inscription for his father, posthumously enfeoffed Governor of Danzhou Zhi. When Emperor Xuanzong heard of it, he personally wrote the stele title and granted it, reading "Alas, the Tomb of Accumulated Goodness."
translations.idiomatic: Yue once composed the stele inscription for his father, Zhi, posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Danzhou. When the emperor heard of it, he personally wrote the stele title and granted it: "Alas, the Tomb of Accumulated Goodness."

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works comprised thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 太常謚議曰「文貞」，左司郎中陽伯誠駁議，以爲不稱，工部侍郎張九齡立議，請依太常爲定，紛綸未決。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous title Wen Zhen; Left Department Director Yang Bocheng submitted a counter-proposal, holding it unsuitable; Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jiuling submitted an opinion requesting that the Minister of Ceremonies' proposal be adopted; debate continued without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous title Wen Zhen. Left Department Director Yang Bocheng objected that it was unsuitable, while Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jiuling argued that the Minister of Ceremonies' proposal should stand. Debate continued without resolution.

sentences.zh: 玄宗爲説自制神道碑文，御筆賜謚曰「文貞」，由是方定。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong personally composed the spirit-way stele inscription for Yue and by his own hand granted the posthumous title Wen Zhen; only then was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong personally composed Yue's spirit-way stele inscription and in his own hand granted the posthumous title Wen Zhen, settling the matter.

sentences.zh: 説子 均均、垍皆能文。

translations.literal: Yue's sons Jun and Jiao were both skilled in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's sons Jun and Jiao were both accomplished writers.

sentences.zh: 説在中書，兄弟已掌綸翰之任。

translations.literal: When Yue was in the Secretariat, the brothers already held charge of imperial drafting.
translations.idiomatic: While Yue served in the Secretariat, the brothers already held charge of imperial drafting.

sentences.zh: 居父憂服闋，均除戸部侍郎，轉兵部。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, Jun was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun's mourning for his father ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and then transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，坐累貶饒州刺史，以太子左庶子征，復爲戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was demoted for accumulated offenses to prefect of Raozhou, then summoned as Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent and again made Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was demoted for accumulated offenses to prefect of Raozhou, then recalled as Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent and restored as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九載，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 自以才名當爲宰輔，常爲李林甫所抑。

translations.literal: He considered his talent and reputation fit for the chief ministership and was constantly suppressed by Li Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: He believed his talent and reputation qualified him for the chief ministership, but Li Linfu constantly blocked him.

sentences.zh: 及林甫卒，依附權臣陳希烈，期於必取。

translations.literal: When Linfu died, he attached himself to the powerful minister Chen Xilie, expecting to obtain the post for certain.
translations.idiomatic: After Linfu died, he attached himself to the powerful minister Chen Xilie, expecting to secure the post.

sentences.zh: 既而楊國忠用事，心頗惡之，罷希烈知政事，引文部侍郎韋見素代之，仍以均爲大理卿。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Guozhong came to power, disliked him in heart, removed Xilie from managing affairs of state, brought in Vice Director of the Secretariat Wei Jiansu to replace him, and still made Jun Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Guozhong came to power and took a strong dislike to him. He removed Xilie from governance, brought in Vice Director of the Secretariat Wei Jiansu to replace him, and made Jun Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 均大失望，意常郁郁。

translations.literal: Jun was greatly disappointed and often depressed in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was deeply disappointed and often despondent.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，受偽命爲中書令，掌賊樞衡。

translations.literal: During the Lushan rebellion he accepted a false appointment as Director of the Secretariat and managed the rebels' central administration.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion he accepted a false appointment as Director of the Secretariat and managed the rebels' central administration.

sentences.zh: 李峴、呂諲條疏陷賊官，均當大辟。

translations.literal: Li Xian and Lu Jin listed and categorized officials who had joined the rebels; Jun deserved the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian and Lu Jin listed officials who had joined the rebels; Jun was judged deserving of death.

sentences.zh: 肅宗於説有舊恩，特免死，長流合浦郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong, owing old favor to Yue, specially spared him from death and banished him for life to Hepu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong, out of old regard for Yue, specially spared Jun from death and banished him for life to Hepu commandery.

sentences.zh: 説子 垍垍，以主婿，玄宗特深恩寵，許於禁中置內宅，侍爲文章，嘗賜珍玩，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Yue's son Jiao, as the emperor's son-in-law, received especially deep favor from Emperor Xuanzong; he was permitted to establish an inner residence in the forbidden palace, attended the emperor in literary matters, and was once given precious curios beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Jiao, as the emperor's son-in-law, received exceptional favor from Emperor Xuanzong. He was permitted to maintain an inner residence in the palace, attended the emperor in literary matters, and received countless precious gifts.

sentences.zh: 時兄均亦供奉翰林院，常以所賜示均，均戲謂垍曰：「此婦翁與女婿，非天子賜學士也。

translations.literal: At that time his elder brother Jun also served in the Hanlin Academy; Jiao often showed Jun what he had been given, and Jun jokingly said to Jiao, "This is father-in-law and son-in-law, not the Son of Heaven giving gifts to a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his elder brother Jun also served in the Hanlin Academy. Jiao often showed Jun what he had received, and Jun joked to Jiao, "These are gifts between father-in-law and son-in-law, not the emperor bestowing favors on a scholar.

sentences.zh: 」天寶中，玄宗嘗幸垍內宅，謂垍曰：「希烈累辭機務，朕擇其代者，孰可？

translations.literal: " During the Tianbao era Emperor Xuanzong once visited Jiao's inner residence and said to him, "Xilie has repeatedly declined confidential affairs; I am choosing his replacement—who would be suitable?
translations.idiomatic: " During the Tianbao reign Emperor Xuanzong once visited Jiao's inner residence and said, "Xilie has repeatedly declined confidential duties. I am choosing his replacement—who would be suitable?

sentences.zh: 」垍錯愕未對，帝即曰：「無逾吾愛婿矣。

translations.literal: " Jiao, startled and confused, did not reply; the emperor at once said, "None surpasses my beloved son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao, startled, did not reply. The emperor at once said, "None surpasses my beloved son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 」垍降階陳謝。

translations.literal: " Jiao descended the steps and expressed thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao descended the steps and expressed his thanks.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠聞而惡之，及希烈罷相，舉韋見素代，垍深觖望。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong heard of this and hated it; when Xilie was removed as chief minister and Wei Jiansu was recommended to replace him, Jiao was deeply disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong heard of this and resented it. When Xilie was removed as chief minister and Wei Jiansu was chosen to replace him, Jiao was deeply embittered.

sentences.zh: 正月，范陽節度使安祿山入朝。

translations.literal: In the first month the Fanyang military governor An Lushan came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month the Fanyang military governor An Lushan came to court.

sentences.zh: 時祿山立破奚、契丹功，尤加寵異。

translations.literal: At that time Lushan had recently achieved merit in defeating the Xi and Khitan and received especially lavish favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had recently won merit by defeating the Xi and Khitan and received especially lavish favor.

sentences.zh: 祿山求帶平章事，下中書擬議。

translations.literal: Lushan requested the concurrent title of Co-Drafter of the Secretariat, and the matter was sent down to the Secretariat for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan requested the concurrent title of Co-Drafter of the Secretariat, and the matter was sent to the Secretariat for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 國忠進言曰：「祿山誠立軍功，然眼不識字，制命若行，臣恐四夷輕國。

translations.literal: Guozhong advanced and said, "Lushan has indeed achieved military merit, yet he cannot even recognize written characters; if such an appointment is issued, your subject fears the four barbarians will look down on the state.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong said, "Lushan has indeed won military merit, yet he cannot even read. If such an appointment is issued, I fear the foreign peoples will look down on the empire.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗乃止，加左僕射而已。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanzong then stopped the appointment and made him only Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanzong then stopped the appointment and made him Left Vice Director only.

sentences.zh: 及祿山還鎮，命中官高力士餞於浐坡。

translations.literal: When Lushan returned to his command, the emperor ordered the palace eunuch Gao Lishi to give a farewell feast at Chan Slope.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan returned to his command, the emperor ordered the palace eunuch Gao Lishi to give a farewell feast at Chan Slope.

sentences.zh: 既還，帝曰：「祿山慰意否？

translations.literal: After he returned, the emperor said, "Was Lushan satisfied?
translations.idiomatic: When Lishi returned, the emperor asked, "Was Lushan satisfied?

sentences.zh: 」力士曰：「觀其深心郁郁，必伺知宰相之命不行故也。

translations.literal: " Lishi said, "Observing his inner heart, he was gloomy; he must have learned that the chief minister's appointment did not go through.
translations.idiomatic: " Lishi said, "He seemed deeply gloomy. He must have learned that the chief minister's appointment did not go through.

sentences.zh: 」帝告國忠，國忠曰：「此議他人不知，必張垍所告。

translations.literal: " The emperor told Guozhong; Guozhong said, "Others did not know of this deliberation—it must have been Zhang Jiao who informed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor told Guozhong. Guozhong said, "No one else knew of this deliberation—it must have been Zhang Jiao who told him.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，盡逐張垍兄弟。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry and drove out all the Zhang brothers.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was enraged and drove out all the Zhang brothers.

sentences.zh: 出均爲建安太守，垍爲盧溪郡司馬，埱爲宜春郡司馬。

translations.literal: Jun was sent out as prefect of Jian'an, Jiao as military aide of Luxi commandery, and Shang as military aide of Yichun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was sent out as prefect of Jian'an, Jiao as military aide of Luxi commandery, and Shang as military aide of Yichun commandery.

sentences.zh: 歳中召還，再遷爲太常卿。

translations.literal: Within the year they were recalled, and Jiao was transferred again to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year Jiao was recalled and again promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀，宰相韋見素、楊國忠、御史大夫魏方進等從，朝臣多不至。

translations.literal: During the Lushan rebellion Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu; chief ministers Wei Jiansu, Yang Guozhong, Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin, and others followed, while many court officials did not come.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu. Chief ministers Wei Jiansu, Yang Guozhong, Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin, and others followed him, while many court officials did not.

sentences.zh: 次咸陽，帝謂高力士曰：「昨日蒼黃離京，朝官不知所詣，今日誰當至者？

translations.literal: Stopping at Xianyang, the emperor said to Gao Lishi, "Yesterday we left the capital in haste; court officials did not know where to go—who should arrive today?
translations.idiomatic: Stopping at Xianyang, the emperor said to Gao Lishi, "Yesterday we left the capital in haste and officials did not know where to go. Who should arrive today?

sentences.zh: 」力士曰：「張垍兄弟世受國恩，又連戚屬，必當先至。

translations.literal: " Lishi said, "The Zhang brothers have received the state's favor for generations and are connected by marriage—they will surely arrive first.
translations.idiomatic: " Lishi said, "The Zhang brothers have received the state's favor for generations and are connected by marriage. They will surely arrive first.

sentences.zh: 房琯素有宰相望，深爲祿山所器，必不此來。

translations.literal: Fang Guan has long had the reputation of a chief minister and is deeply valued by Lushan—he will surely not come here.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan has long been regarded as chief-minister material and is highly valued by Lushan. He will surely not come.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「事未可料。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "The matter cannot yet be predicted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "That remains to be seen.

sentences.zh: 」是日，琯至，帝大悅，因問均、垍，琯曰：「臣離京時，亦過其舍，比約同行，均報雲『已於城南取馬』。

translations.literal: " That day Fang Guan arrived; the emperor was greatly pleased and then asked about Jun and Jiao. Guan said, "When I left the capital I also passed their residence; we had arranged to travel together, but Jun replied, 'I have already gone to the south of the city to fetch horses.'
translations.idiomatic: " That day Fang Guan arrived. The emperor was greatly pleased and asked about Jun and Jiao. Guan said, "When I left the capital I stopped at their residence. We had arranged to travel together, but Jun replied that he had already gone south of the city to fetch horses.

sentences.zh: 觀其趣向，來意不切。

translations.literal: Judging by his inclination, his intent to come was not earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by his behavior, he had no real intention of coming.

sentences.zh: 」既而均弟兄果受祿山偽命，垍與陳希烈爲賊宰相，垍死於賊中。

translations.literal: " Before long Jun and his brothers indeed accepted false appointments from Lushan; Jiao and Chen Xilie became rebel chief ministers, and Jiao died among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Jun and his brothers did accept false appointments from Lushan. Jiao and Chen Xilie became rebel chief ministers, and Jiao died among the rebels.

sentences.zh: 附 陳希烈陳希烈者，宋州人也。

translations.literal: Appendix: Chen Xilie—Chen Xilie was a man of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Chen Xilie was a native of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 精玄學，書無不覽。

translations.literal: He was skilled in arcane learning and read every book without exception.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in arcane learning and had read widely in every field.

sentences.zh: 開元中，玄宗留意經義，自褚無量、元行沖卒後，得希烈與鳳翔人馮朝隱，常於禁中講《老》、《易》。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era Emperor Xuanzong devoted attention to classical meaning; after Chu Wuliang and Yuan Xingchong died, he obtained Xilie and Feng Chaoyin of Fengxiang, who often lectured on the Laozi and the Book of Changes within the forbidden palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign Emperor Xuanzong devoted attention to classical learning. After Chu Wuliang and Yuan Xingchong died, he found Xilie and Feng Chaoyin of Fengxiang, who often lectured on the Laozi and the Book of Changes within the palace.

sentences.zh: 累遷至秘書少監，代張九齡專判集賢院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in turn to Vice Director of the Secretariat Library and replaced Zhang Jiuling in sole charge of the affairs of the Academy of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Vice Director of the Secretariat Library and replaced Zhang Jiuling in sole charge of the Academy of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 玄宗凡有撰述，必經希烈之手。

translations.literal: Whatever Emperor Xuanzong composed necessarily passed through Xilie's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Every composition of Emperor Xuanzong passed through Xilie's hands.

sentences.zh: 李林甫知上睠待深異，又以和裕易制，乃引爲宰相，同知政事，相行甚歡。

translations.literal: Li Linfu knew that the emperor's regard for him was exceptionally deep and that he was gentle, generous, and easy to control; he therefore brought him in as chief minister to manage affairs of state together, and the two got on very well.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu knew the emperor favored Xilie deeply and that he was gentle and easy to control. He therefore brought him in as chief minister to share governance, and the two got on very well.

sentences.zh: 而林甫居位日久，雖陰謀奸畫足以自固，亦希烈佐佑唱和之力也。

translations.literal: Yet though Linfu held office for a long time and his secret plots and treacherous schemes were enough to secure himself, this was also due to the force of Xilie's support and cooperation.
translations.idiomatic: Though Linfu held office for a long time and his secret schemes were enough to secure his position, this was also due to Xilie's support and cooperation.

sentences.zh: 累遷兼兵部尚書、左相，封潁川郡開國公，寵遇侔於林甫。

translations.literal: He was promoted in turn to concurrent Minister of War and Left Chief Minister, enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan commandery, and received favor equal to Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to concurrent Minister of War and Left Chief Minister, was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan, and received favor equal to Linfu.

sentences.zh: 及林甫死，楊國忠用事，素忌嫉之。

translations.literal: When Linfu died, Yang Guozhong came to power and had long envied and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Linfu died, Yang Guozhong came to power and had long envied him.

sentences.zh: 乃引韋見素同列，罷希烈知政事，守太子太師。

translations.literal: He therefore brought in Wei Jiansu as a colleague, removed Xilie from managing affairs of state, and had him serve as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Wei Jiansu as a colleague, removed Xilie from governance, and had him serve as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 希烈失恩，心頗怏怏。

translations.literal: Xilie lost favor and was rather resentful in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie lost favor and grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，與張垍、達奚珣同掌賊之機衡。

translations.literal: During the Lushan rebellion he, together with Zhang Jiao and Daxi Xun, jointly managed the rebels' central administration.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion he, together with Zhang Jiao and Daxi Xun, jointly managed the rebels' central administration.

sentences.zh: 六等定罪，希烈當斬，肅宗以上皇素遇，賜死於家。

translations.literal: Under the six-rank system of sentencing, Xilie deserved execution; Emperor Suzong, because the Retired Emperor had long favored him, granted him death at home.
translations.idiomatic: Under the six-rank system of sentencing, Xilie deserved execution. Emperor Suzong, because the Retired Emperor had long favored him, granted him death at home.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：劉徐公負不羈之材，逢抵巇之運，遂能奮命決策，扶力中興，朝爲徒步之人，夕據公侯之位，茍非輕死重利，不恥不義之富，安及此哉！

translations.literal: The historian remarks: The historian remarks: Duke Liu of Xu possessed an untamed talent and met a perilous age; he was therefore able to exert his life in decision-making and support the restoration of the dynasty—from a man on foot in the morning to one holding the rank of duke or marquis by evening. If he had not held death lightly and profit dearly, and had not disdained unrighteous wealth, how could he have reached this!
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Duke Liu of Xu possessed untamed talent and met a perilous age. He was able to risk his life in decisive action and help restore the dynasty—from a commoner in the morning to a noble by evening. Had he not held death lightly and profit dearly, and disdained unrighteous wealth, how could he have reached such heights?

sentences.zh: 郭代公、張燕公解逢掖而登將壇，驅貔虎之師，斷獯戎之臂，暨居衡軸，克致隆平，可謂武緯文經，惟申與甫而已。

translations.literal: Duke Guo of Dai and Duke Zhang of Yan left the scholar's robe and ascended the general's platform, drove armies like tigers and leopards, severed the arms of the Xiongnu barbarians, and when they reached the pivot of government achieved abundant peace—this may be called combining military and civil excellence; only Shen and Fu compare.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Guo of Dai and Duke Zhang of Yan left the scholar's robe for the general's platform, commanded armies like tigers and leopards, and broke the power of the northern barbarians. When they reached the helm of state they helped bring about an age of peace. They combined military and civil excellence as few have—only Yi Yin and Yan Ying compare.

sentences.zh: 惜乎均、垍務速，失節賊廷。

translations.literal: Alas, Jun and Jiao sought advancement too hastily and lost their integrity in the rebel court.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Jun and Jiao sought advancement too hastily and lost their integrity in the rebel court.

sentences.zh: 自武德已來，稱賢相者，房、杜、姚、宋四公，皆遭無賴子弟汙圮先業，非獨燕國之不幸也。

translations.literal: Since the Wude era, of those called worthy chief ministers—the four lords Fang, Du, Yao, and Song—all suffered worthless sons who defiled and ruined their fathers' achievements; this was not the misfortune of the State of Yan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wude era, the four chief ministers widely called worthy—Fang, Du, Yao, and Song—all suffered worthless sons who ruined their fathers' achievements. This was not the misfortune of the House of Yan alone.

sentences.zh: 希烈柔而多智，長於名理，竟死於名。

translations.literal: Xilie was gentle and very clever, excelled in the logic of names, and in the end died because of reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was gentle and clever, excelled in philosophical disputation, and in the end died because of reputation.

sentences.zh: 所謂離婁不見其眉睫，與夫平叔、太初，同膏肓耳。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by Li Lou not seeing his own eyebrows and eyelashes—like Ping Shu and Taichu, he shared the same fatal blindness.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by the saying that even Li Lou cannot see his own eyebrows—like He Yan and Xi Kang, he suffered the same fatal blindness.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：箕、微去紂，閎、散扶昌。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The eulogy says: Jizi and Weizi left King Zhou; Hong Yao and San Yisheng supported the rise of the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Jizi and Weizi left King Zhou; Hong Yao and San Yisheng supported the rise of the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 謀不近義，旋踵而亡。

translations.literal: Plots that do not cleave to righteousness perish in the turning of a heel.
translations.idiomatic: Plots that stray from righteousness perish in an instant.

sentences.zh: 幽求不令，道濟允臧。

translations.literal: Youqiu was not virtuous; Daoji was truly good.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu lacked virtue; Daoji was truly worthy.

sentences.zh: 偉哉郭侯，勛德煌煌。

translations.literal: Grand is Marquis Guo—his merit and virtue blaze brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Grand is Marquis Guo—his merit and virtue shine brilliantly.
